mnemonic: The sushi chef asks whose order it is. Every hand goes up, so you jab a thumb into your own chest: "I want a sushi." Wa-ta-shi. わたし.
notes: Can also be read わたくし (very formal) or あたし (feminine, casual). There are rarer readings too. 僕 ぼく is the male, less formal one.
sentence: 私はアンです。
sentence_meaning: I am Ann.

meaning: you (usually when one doesn't know the person)
mnemonic: The prize-giver hasn't learned a single name all night. Another. Another. Every time the finger lands on a stranger, that's what they get. あなた.
notes: Neutral, and the one that turns up where you do not know the person. 君 きみ is spoken downward, to somebody younger or junior.
sentence: あなたはトムさんですか。
sentence_meaning: Are you Tom-san?

mnemonic: Nobody has ever shortened the sun's name. Emperors bow to it, farmers thank it, no one calls it Sunny. さん on a name is that same small bow, every time.
notes: The most common neutral polite honorific, similar to using 'Mr/Ms' before a name in English.
sentence: あなたはトムさんですか。
sentence_meaning: Are you Tom-san?

mnemonic: In the tannery one figure steps (彳) between the hanging skins (皮) all day and never gives a name. Not you, not her, just him. Moves like karate: かれ.
notes: The character also carried an old sense of that, which is why the breakdown reads he, that. As a word it only ever means he.
sentence: 彼はトムさんです。
sentence_meaning: He is Tom-san.

mnemonic: 女 woman, 子 child: the shape is someone holding what they love most. And what she loves is one more run in the dark after the lifts stop, "ski." すき.
notes: Grammatically not a verb, though it's often translated into English as 'to like'.
sentence: 私はワインが好きです。
sentence_meaning: I like wine.

mnemonic: On a packed train a heel comes down on your toe and you surface ready to fight. It's just a bloke, wincing back at you. Heel, toe. ひと.
notes: Same kanji as 人 じん, which only ever hangs off the end of a country name. ひと is the standalone word for a person. 方 かた is the polite word for a person and 者 もの the plainer one.
sentence: あの人はいい人です。
sentence_meaning: That person is a good person.

mnemonic: The spoon goes in and the chef says nothing, just a long rising "eeee", eyes shut, one hand up to stop you talking. He never finds a word. いい.
notes: Good in itself. 上手い うまい is good at something, a skill.
sentence: あの人はいい人です。
sentence_meaning: That person is a good person.

mnemonic: He shakes your hand before you've asked anything: "Jin. Nihon-jin." Name and country welded together. A country plus じん is a person from there.
notes: Used as a suffix on a country name to mean a person from that country, e.g. 日本人 nihonjin.
sentence: 私はイギリス人です。
sentence_meaning: I am British.

mnemonic: No pun here, just two parts. 日本 is Japan, ご is "language of". Bolt them together and you have にほんご. Every language works the same way.
sentence: 私は日本語を勉強しています。
sentence_meaning: I'm studying Japanese.

mnemonic: 勉 is exemption (免) won by force (力), 強 is strength. Ben moved to Kyoto to grind out both and still hasn't sat the exam. Ben-Kyo: べんきょう.
sentence: 私は日本語を勉強しています。
sentence_meaning: I'm studying Japanese.

mnemonic: 木 a tree with 一 a line struck across its root. The origin a thing grows from, and what books are made of. Hone your mind on one: ほん.
sentence: いい本でしたね。
sentence_meaning: It was a good book, wasn't it?

mnemonic: こ- marks whatever is nearest me, so これ is the thing in my own hand. Hold up the apple core you're still holding: core, これ.
notes: One of the こ/そ/あ/ど set: こ near me, そ near you, あ away from us both, ど the question.
sentence: これは日本語の本です。
sentence_meaning: This is a Japanese book.

mnemonic: 亻 a person next to 可 "can". Someone demanding to know what can possibly be going on. The nanny throws up her hands: what?! なに.
notes: Can be read either なに or なん depending on what follows.
sentence: A「これは何ですか。」B「本です。」
sentence_meaning: A: What is this?B: It's a book.

mnemonic: そ- marks whatever is near you rather than me, so それ is that thing by your elbow. Point at the sore on it: sore, それ.
notes: The plain that. 彼 かれ shares the gloss because its character once meant that, but the word itself only means he.
sentence: それは本です。
sentence_meaning: That is a book.

mnemonic: あ- is the far one, away from us both. あれ is the thing across the road, too distant to name, so you just ask what those ARE. あれ.
notes: あれ stands on its own. あの has to be followed by a noun: あの人, that person.
sentence: あれは何ですか。
sentence_meaning: What's that?

mnemonic: ど- always marks the question. Five identical doors, no labels, and you still have to choose one of them: which? Door, どれ.
notes: どれ picks one out of a set you can both see. 何 なに asks with nothing laid out.
sentence: どれが好きですか。
sentence_meaning: Which would you like?

mnemonic: 毎 is 母 mother with a stroke through her, 日 is the sun. Mother, at every single sunrise, without fail. My knee aches at each one: まいにち.
sentence: 毎日、日本語を勉強します。
sentence_meaning: I study Japanese every day.

mnemonic: 口 a mouth on 儿 two legs. A boy who is mostly mouth, and older than you. He lost a bet and has been called Annie ever since: あに.
sentence: これは兄のパソコンです。
sentence_meaning: This is my older brother's personal computer.

mnemonic: An ear twitches above the long grass. You can't see the rabbit, but the ear is proof something alive is in there. いる is for things that breathe.
notes: いる for anything alive, ある for everything else. A cat いる in the room and the chair ある in it.
sentence: 兄がいます。
sentence_meaning: I have an older brother.

mnemonic: Rocks don't twitch or breathe. They are simply there, and the most you can say is that they ARE. ある is existence with no pulse in it.
notes: ある for things, いる for anything alive. Between them they cover the whole job of existing.
sentence: ペンがある。
sentence_meaning: There is a pen.

mnemonic: One dry sliver of Mary's cake is left and nobody is reaching for it. Not very much, and not very good. A-Mary: あまり.
notes: Almost always paired with a negative, あまり…ない, "not very…".
sentence: スポーツはあまり好きじゃありません。
sentence_meaning: I don't really like sports.

mnemonic: A lid pulled shut over a single stroke, this one moment, sealed off from every other. Emma wants you at the table now: いま.
notes: The everyday now. 現在 げんざい is the formal one, for temperatures, records and announcements.
sentence: 彼は今、勉強しています。
sentence_meaning: He's studying now.

mnemonic: 日 the sun in a 寺 temple, then 日 the sun in a 門 gate. Time is the sun crossing something. Genghis Khan checks his watch: じかん.
sentence: 今は時間がありません。
sentence_meaning: I don't have time now.

mnemonic: 灬 four fire-dots under the whole tangle above them, burning until not one stroke is left. Bill Nye vanishes mid-sentence: ない.
notes: Often used as the negative form of ある. Worth checking a grammar reference for full usage.
sentence: 今はあまり時間が無いのです。
sentence_meaning: I don't have much time now.

mnemonic: こ- is the near one again, but この always needs a noun behind it, this cone, this book. It points first and names second. この.
sentence: 山田さんの本はどれですか。この本ですか。
sentence_meaning: Which book is Yamada-san's? Is it this book?

mnemonic: そ- is yours rather than mine, and その needs a noun too. Sonic points down at the one by your foot: that book, not this one. その.
sentence: その本ですか。
sentence_meaning: Is it that book?

mnemonic: あ- is far from both of us, so あの book is the one on the other shelf and you both have to turn to look. Ah, no, further: あの.
notes: あの has to sit in front of a noun. あれ is the one that stands alone.
sentence: あの本ですか。
sentence_meaning: That book (over there)?

mnemonic: ど- asks the question. A shelf of identical spines, dough all over your hands, and you still have to point at one of them: どの.
sentence: どの本ですか。
sentence_meaning: Which book is it?

mnemonic: 目 an eye up on 儿 two legs, wandering about looking at things. It stops in front of a mirror and finally sees itself: みる.
sentence: 兄は毎日テレビを見ます。
sentence_meaning: My older brother watches TV every day.

mnemonic: 全 is 王 a king under 𠆢 one roof: everything. 然 is 犬 dog meat over 灬 fire. Burn the whole lot and there is nothing left at all: ぜんぜん.
notes: Usually paired with a negative, though colloquially it also turns up with positives.
sentence: テレビを全然見ません。
sentence_meaning: I never watch television.

mnemonic: 面 a face gone 白 white. Someone so gripped by the thing that the blood has drained out of them. Oh, Moe, Shirley: おもしろい.
sentence: この本は全然面白くなかった。
sentence_meaning: This book wasn't interesting at all.

mnemonic: The verb that does anything at all: bolt it onto a noun and the noun becomes an action, tennis, study, whatever. Sue me if I don't: する.
sentence: 彼はテニスをします。
sentence_meaning: He plays tennis (lit: "He does tennis").

meaning: to become, to result in, to come (to do)
mnemonic: The sea was flat this morning. All afternoon the waves grew, and by evening they are gnarly. It did not start that way, it became that way: なる.
notes: Has many meanings and shades of use ('to become', 'to result in', 'to come to do'). It takes time to fully absorb.
sentence: 日本語の勉強が好きになりました。
sentence_meaning: I have come to like Japanese study.

mnemonic: 先 is someone striding out ahead of you, 生 is life itself. The one who went first and has already lived it, sensei: せんせい.
sentence: 私は日本語の先生になりたいです。
sentence_meaning: I want to become a Japanese teacher.

mnemonic: Kneel, sigh, and hold the pose: coo-da-sigh. Hang it on a noun or a て-form verb and the whole thing turns into a request. ください.
sentence: コーヒーをください。
sentence_meaning: Please give me a coffee.

mnemonic: 名 is 夕 an evening with 口 a mouth. Calling out into the dark to find who's there. 前 is what comes first, and what comes back is なまえ.
notes: The noun. 呼ぶ よぶ is the verb, calling somebody by it.
sentence: あなたの名前を教えてください。
sentence_meaning: Please tell me your name.

mnemonic: 孝 devotion to your elders, next to 攵 a stick to rap you with. That was teaching, once. Oh, she'll teach you one way or another: おしえる.
sentence: あなたの名前を教えてください。
sentence_meaning: Please tell me your name.

mnemonic: こ- always marks the near one, so ここ is the ground under your own feet. He puts the stick down and taps twice, hard. Not there. Here. Here: ここ.
notes: Plain here. こちら is the polite version, and doubles as this way.
sentence: ここに本があります。
sentence_meaning: There's a book here.

mnemonic: そ- is your side of the room rather than mine, so そこ is where you're standing. The socket by your foot, not the one by mine: そこ.
sentence: そこはトイレです。
sentence_meaning: There is the bathroom.

mnemonic: あ- is far from us both, so あそこ is the socket on the far wall. Ah, that socket, the one neither of us can reach from here: あそこ.
sentence: 彼はあそこにいます。
sentence_meaning: He is over there.

mnemonic: ど- is the question again. You put the dough down somewhere in this kitchen and now not one person can find it. Where? どこ.
sentence: あの本をどこに置きましたか。
sentence_meaning: Where did you put that book?

mnemonic: 罒 an eye above 直 straight, setting something down and lining it up dead level. You place the cup on the oak table: おく.
notes: The verb. ところ and 場所 ばしょ are the nouns for a place.
sentence: あの本をどこに置きましたか。
sentence_meaning: Where did you put that book?

mnemonic: 宀 a roof with 豕 a pig underneath it. That is what a house was: the animals in out of the rain. Walk in, drop the bags, sigh, yeah: いえ.
notes: Can also be read うち in certain contexts.
sentence: ここが私の家です。
sentence_meaning: This is my house.

mnemonic: That is a broom (帚) on the right, and it is the whole point: sweep up, then head back where you came from. Carry your bags in: かえる.
sentence: 家に帰ろう。
sentence_meaning: Let's go home.

mnemonic: 言 speech with 舌 a tongue right beside it, words with a tongue doing all the work. Hannah, she talked the whole night: はなし.
sentence: あなたの話は面白いね。
sentence_meaning: Your story is interesting.

mnemonic: 矢 an arrow and 口 a mouth: the answer out fast and straight, no hesitation. That's the difference between guessing and knowing. Sure: しる.
sentence: あの人を知っていますか。
sentence_meaning: Do you know that person?

mnemonic: 彼 him with 女 woman bolted onto the end, the same word, other half. She brings you a can o' Joe every single morning: かのじょ.
sentence: 彼女の名前を知っていますか。
sentence_meaning: Do you know her name?

mnemonic: Tack it onto a name and the name gets smaller and fonder at the same time. Your little sister is Jackie Chan for the afternoon: ちゃん.
notes: An honorific usually used to show endearment, especially with girls and small children.
sentence: 彼女はララちゃんです。
sentence_meaning: She is Lara-chan.

mnemonic: Someone asks and you don't leave a gap, you throw a bale of hay in the air and shout it. High, hay, はい. That's the sound of yes.
sentence: A「山田さんですか。」B「はい。」
sentence_meaning: A: Are you Yamada-san?B: Yes, I am.

mnemonic: いい means good, so いいえ ought to mean better. It doesn't. Gloomy Eeyore says no to everything, including that: いいえ.
sentence: A「山田さんですか。」B「いいえ。」
sentence_meaning: A: Are you Yamada-san?B: No, I'm not.

mnemonic: 日 the sun and 本 the origin: the place the sun starts out from. Land of the rising sun, said in two characters. にほん.
notes: Can be read either にほん or にっぽん.
sentence: 日本のゲームは面白いです。
sentence_meaning: Japanese games are fun.

mnemonic: 学 a child under a roof learning, 校 a 木 tree where the paths 交 cross. Somewhere in it a cuckoo clock rings to let you out: がっこう.
sentence: 学校は日本にあります。
sentence_meaning: The school is in Japan.

mnemonic: 行 is a crossroads from above, and its left half is 彳, the same step radical as 彼. Stood at the junction you have to move: eek, いく.
sentence: 学校へ行きます。
sentence_meaning: I will go to school.

mnemonic: 明 is 日 sun and 月 moon side by side: bright. Add another 日 and you have the next bright morning. A cheetah gets there first: あした.
sentence: 明日、学校へ行きます。
sentence_meaning: Tomorrow, I will go to school.

mnemonic: The old shape was wheat standing in a field, and nothing about it moves. You stay exactly where you are and by August the whole crew has arrived: くる.
notes: Arriving. なる なる shares the gloss only because it turns up as to come to do something.
sentence: 明日、来ますか。
sentence_meaning: Will you come tomorrow?

mnemonic: It doesn't matter how many times you've already done it, you are doing it again tomorrow and the day after that. Matter: また.
sentence: 明日、また来ます。
sentence_meaning: I'll come again tomorrow.

mnemonic: There is only one thing anyone actually wants to know about a deadline, and it isn't what or why. When is it due? It's-due: いつ.
sentence: 彼女はいつ来ますか。
sentence_meaning: When is she coming?

mnemonic: 田 a field sat on 心 a heart, thinking happens in the chest here, not the head. Moe leans on the bar working something out: おもう.
notes: What you feel or reckon, without working at it. 考える かんがえる is thinking a thing through on purpose.
sentence: これがいいと思います。
sentence_meaning: I think this is good.

mnemonic: こ- is near me, so こう is my way of doing it: like this, watch. The coach demonstrates once and expects you to copy it: こう.
sentence: こうしましょう。
sentence_meaning: Let’s do this (“this way”).

mnemonic: そ- is your side, so そう is your way of putting it. That's so, that's how you see it. And I think so too: そう.
sentence: 私もそう思います。
sentence_meaning: That's what I think too.

mnemonic: ど- is the question, so どう asks about the manner of a thing: how? Dough all over your hands and no idea how much you actually need: どう.
notes: どう asks about manner, how a thing is or goes. 何 なに asks which thing it is.
sentence: あなたはどう思いますか。
sentence_meaning: What do you think?

mnemonic: 会 is a roof with people gathering in underneath it. You meet this one by walking straight into them on the way in, ow: あう.
notes: Same reading as 合う あう, to fit. 会う is meeting a person; 合う is things matching. 出会う であう is running into somebody by chance.
sentence: 明日、彼と会います。
sentence_meaning: I will meet him tomorrow.

mnemonic: 冫 ice beside 欠 a yawn. Waiting your turn in a cold queue. The next donut along is still too gooey to pick up: つぎ.
sentence: 次はいつ会いましょうか。
sentence_meaning: When next shall we meet?

mnemonic: Point the hoe wherever you want the row to run. 方 is which way a thing faces, not the thing itself: ほう.
notes: Same kanji as 方 かた "person (polite)". This reading is the direction, not the person.
sentence: 彼は私の方を見ました。
sentence_meaning: He looked in my direction.

mnemonic: The same 方, read かた. Instead of pointing at a person you gesture their way, "the next one, please." Said mid karate kata: かた.
notes: Same kanji as ほう "direction", pointing politely rather than naming. As a word for a person this is the polite one. 人 ひと is neutral and 者 もの is blunter.
sentence: 次の方、どうぞ。
sentence_meaning: The next person, please.

mnemonic: 門 a gate with 耳 an ear pressed right into it. Someone kicks the gate and the ear behind it hears every bit of it: きく.
notes: Identical to 聞く "to ask". Context decides which.
sentence: 彼女はラジオを聞いています。
sentence_meaning: She's listening to the radio.

mnemonic: Same gate, same ear. You can kick it to hear what's inside, or kick it to get an answer out. Hearing and asking are one verb: きく.
notes: Identical to 聞く "to hear". Context decides which.
sentence: トムに聞いて。
sentence_meaning: Ask Tom.

mnemonic: 願 is 原 a plain with 頁 a head bowed low over it, wishing hard. Oh, negate the no, she must say yes: おねがいします.
notes: The everyday please when you want something. 何とか is please as in somehow, find a way.
sentence: A「これでお願いします。」B「はい。」
sentence_meaning: A: This one, please.B: Okay.

mnemonic: 分 is 八 splitting with 刀 a blade, cutting a thing into pieces small enough to see. A wacky kangaroo finally splits it for you: わかる.
sentence: 日本語のニュースが全然分かりませんでした。
sentence_meaning: I didn't understand the Japanese news at all.

mnemonic: The yolk is the good part of the egg, and eating it well means finishing it properly. Sat in front of a verb, よく means doing it well.
notes: Same word as よく "often". The verb it modifies decides which.
sentence: よく分かりました。
sentence_meaning: I understood well.

mnemonic: Same よく, same yolk. Except you have one every single morning. It means well or often depending on the verb behind it: よく.
notes: Same word as よく "well". The verb it modifies decides which.
sentence: ジャズのCDをよく聞きます。
sentence_meaning: I listen to Jazz CDs often.

mnemonic: 耂 an old man bent over, taking his time about it. Not a quick thought, a whole conga line of them, shuffled through slowly: かんがえる.
notes: Deliberate, turning it over. 思う おもう is what you already reckon without effort.
sentence: よく考えてください。
sentence_meaning: Please think carefully.

mnemonic: An alligator in a suit bows until his snout hits the floor, and then keeps going. The longer the bow runs the politer it is, and this one is the longest: ありがとうございます.
reading: ありがとうございます
sentence: そうですか。分かりました。ありがとうございます。
sentence_meaning: Is that so? I understand. Thank you.
word: ありがとうございます

mnemonic: Same 話 as the story, but now someone is doing the talking: 言 speech with 舌 a tongue going. Hannah, Sue will speak to you about it: はなす.
sentence: 先生と日本語で話します。
sentence_meaning: I speak Japanese with the teacher.

mnemonic: The family motto is one word long and no amount has ever satisfied it. Whatever is already on the table, the answer comes back もっと.
sentence: もっと勉強しなければいけないと思った。
sentence_meaning: I thought that I would have to study more.

mnemonic: You, and a curry far too hot to rush at. Small spoonfuls, long gaps between them, eyes watering. That pace right there is ゆっくり.
sentence: もっとゆっくり話してください。
sentence_meaning: Please speak more slowly.

mnemonic: 言 is a mouth with the sound drawn coming out of it. Whatever you've just seen, the first thing out is ewww. And you've said it: いう.
sentence: ゆっくり言ってください。
sentence_meaning: Please say it slowly.

mnemonic: 友 is two hands reaching the same way, 達 makes it a group. Toes so attached you keep tripping over each other: ともだち.
sentence: 友達とレストランに行きました。
sentence_meaning: I went to the restaurant with my friend.

mnemonic: 彳 a step outside 寺 a temple. The same two pieces you met in 彼 and 時, now meaning to stand there. Sit on the mat, Sue is late: まつ.
sentence: 1時間友達を待ちました。
sentence_meaning: I waited for my friend for an hour.

mnemonic: 昨 is the day just gone and 日 makes it a day. That key doesn't open anything any more. No, that's yesterday's key: きのう.
sentence: 昨日、友達に会った。
sentence_meaning: I met a friend yesterday.

mnemonic: 田 a field with 丁 a street cut straight through it, which is how a town starts. One road, and once a year the whole place turns out to march down it: まち.
sentence: あの町に行きました。
sentence_meaning: I went to that town over there.

mnemonic: 高 is a tall building drawn in strokes, and a price does the same thing. It goes up. The tag is tacked high on the wall where you have to squint at it: たかい.
notes: Same word as 高い "high, tall", height and price share one adjective.
sentence: このカメラは高いですね。
sentence_meaning: This camera is expensive.

mnemonic: The very same 高い, and one word does the tower and the bill both. Forty floors, and the window cleaner's rate is tacked high by the lift: たかい.
notes: Same word as 高い "expensive", height and price share one adjective.
sentence: これがこの町で一番高いビルです。
sentence_meaning: This is the tallest building in town.

mnemonic: 一 one and 番 a turn in the order: number one in the sequence, so the most of whatever follows. First prize is an itchy golden bun: いちばん.
sentence: これがこの町で一番高いビルです。
sentence_meaning: This is the tallest building in this town.

mnemonic: Charlotte only ever wants a little. A little more, a little longer, a little cheaper, never a lot of anything: ちょっと.
sentence: これはちょっと高いですね。
sentence_meaning: This is a little expensive.

mnemonic: You have already mowed the lawn and it isn't nine o'clock yet. もう marks the thing that got done sooner than anyone expected.
notes: Same word as もう "another, again". Whether it looks back or forward decides which.
sentence: 彼はもう帰りました。
sentence_meaning: He's already gone home.

mnemonic: The same もう, mown again. Pointed forwards instead of backwards it means one more, another slice, a little longer: もうちょっと.
notes: Same word as もう "already". Whether it looks back or forward decides which.
sentence: もうちょっと食べたい。
sentence_meaning: I want to eat a little more.

mnemonic: The old shape is a hand gripping an axe. Your father, mid-swing, cracking the same joke he has told all week: Cheech. ちち.
notes: Your own father, spoken about to other people. 母 はは is the matching word for mother.
sentence: 私は父が大好きです。
sentence_meaning: I love my father.

mnemonic: 大 is a person with both arms flung wide, big. Bolt that onto 好き fondness and you have the full span of it: だいすき.
notes: Everyday, and literally very fond of. 愛する あいする is the heavy one, and not for ice cream.
sentence: 私は父が大好きです。
sentence_meaning: I love my father.

mnemonic: The shape is a woman with the feeding marks drawn in. And she is the one laughing hardest at your terrible joke: haha, はは.
notes: Your own mother, spoken about to other people. 父 ちち is the matching word for father.
sentence: 昨日、母と話をしました。
sentence_meaning: I talked to my mother yesterday.

meaning: to give (receiver is not in the speaker's group)
mnemonic: You hand the parcel outward, away from your own circle, while a jaguar watches from the treeline. あげる is giving that leaves your side.
notes: Contrast with くれる, which is giving that comes toward you and yours.
sentence: 友達にプレゼントをあげます。
sentence_meaning: I will give a present to my friend.

meaning: to give (receiver is in the speaker's group)
mnemonic: The opposite direction to あげる: this one arrives. Someone presses the cure into your hand, ooh. くれる is giving that comes to you.
notes: Direction is the whole distinction: あげる goes out, くれる comes in. 与える あたえる is the formal give, the one that takes abstract objects.
sentence: 父が本をくれました。
sentence_meaning: My father gave me a book.

mnemonic: Presents keep being handed to you and your arms are already full. More, ow. You are the one receiving all of it: もらう.
notes: The plain one, being given something. 受ける is taking what is directed at you, and 受け取る is taking delivery of it.
sentence: 彼女からプレゼントをもらいました。
sentence_meaning: I got a present from her.

mnemonic: 牛 a cow beside 勿. Livestock was once the thing you owned. Now it is any object at all, sorted mono-tonously one by one: もの.
sentence: 色々な物をもらいました。
sentence_meaning: I received many things.

meaning: you (to someone of equal or lower status)
mnemonic: 尹 a hand giving orders over 口 a mouth. Spoken down the ranks, never up. Kimmy, come here. きみ is you to someone below you.
notes: Spoken downward, or between close friends, and it can land blunt. あなた is the neutral one.
sentence: この本を君にあげます。
sentence_meaning: I'm going to give you this book.

mnemonic: A single line driven straight through the centre of a box. Reach into the middle of the nacho bowl for the one underneath: なか.
sentence: 父は家の中にいます。
sentence_meaning: My father is inside the house.

meaning: to be able to do, to be good at
mnemonic: 出 coming out and 来 coming toward. What comes out of you when it is called for. You built the whole deck yourself, ooh: できる.
sentence: あなたはスキーが出来ますか。
sentence_meaning: Can you ski?

mnemonic: 本 the origin and 当 hitting the mark: the version that lands where it started out. Hone in, tow the line. Is it really ほんとう?
sentence: その話は本当ですか。
sentence_meaning: Is that story true?

mnemonic: The shape is a person planted on a line of ground, feet apart. Hold that still while the tattoo needle works and don't flinch: たつ.
sentence: 彼はステージに立った。
sentence_meaning: He stood on stage.

mnemonic: 前 is the part that goes out ahead of everything else. Stood in front of the whole class with your hand up: may I? まえ.
notes: Already met inside 名前. The name that comes first.
sentence: ララちゃんは家の前に立っています。
sentence_meaning: Lara-chan is standing in front of the house.

mnemonic: 入 is a doorway drawn narrowing as it goes in, so you have to duck. You dip your head through it and say hi to the room as you arrive: はいる.
sentence: レストランに入ります。
sentence_meaning: I will enter the restaurant.

mnemonic: 家 the house with the pig under its roof, 族 a clan gathered under one banner. Together they are everyone who lives there: かぞく.
sentence: 家族がテレビを見た。
sentence_meaning: The family watched television.

mnemonic: 亻 a person beside 主 the master of the house. The one who actually lives there rather than the one visiting. He has moved in for good: すむ.
sentence: 家族はタイに住んでいます。
sentence_meaning: My family lives in Thailand.

mnemonic: 大 is a person with both arms flung as wide as they will go, and that is the entire word. Big. Say it long and slow: oh-oh-kee-na, おおきな.
sentence: 大きな家に住みたい。
sentence_meaning: I want to live in a big house.

mnemonic: The same 大, the same big. 大きな and 大きい mean exactly the same thing. This one just ends in い, the way most adjectives do: おおきい.
notes: 大きな sits directly in front of a noun; 大きい behaves like a normal い-adjective.
sentence: 彼は大きい家に住んでいる。
sentence_meaning: He lives in a big house.

mnemonic: Someone calls your name across a crowded room and you have turned round before you even thought about it. That sound arriving is こえ.
sentence: 彼は大きな声で話した。
sentence_meaning: He spoke with a loud voice.

mnemonic: An eye stood up on its end, with the lines of the lid drawn straight across it. Point at one of your own and say the English word "me": め.
sentence: ララちゃんは目が大きいです。
sentence_meaning: Lara-chan has big eyes.

mnemonic: A hand with its fingers drawn out from the wrist. You put it up to answer a question and somebody presses a cup of tea into it: て.
sentence: 分かった人は手を上げてください。
sentence_meaning: The people who understood, please raise your hand.

mnemonic: 上 is a mark sitting above the line, up. Same あげる you already know for giving, except the thing going up is your own hand: あげる.
notes: Same reading as あげる "to give". This one is written with 上 and means to lift. 上がる あがる is the thing going up on its own.
sentence: 分かった人は手を上げてください。
sentence_meaning: The people who understood, please raise your hand.

mnemonic: She is holding two things at once and cannot stand one of them. Whatever it is, she would rather kill it than keep it: きらい.
sentence: 私はタバコが嫌いです。
sentence_meaning: I hate cigarettes.

mnemonic: Oh, jii-san. With the same さん bow on the end you already know from names. He is the old man of the house and he is not moving: おじいさん.
sentence: おじいさんはジョギングが嫌いです。
sentence_meaning: My grandfather dislikes jogging.

mnemonic: Built exactly like おじいさん with baa in place of jii. Oh, baa-san, the old woman of the house, sheep noise included: おばあさん.
sentence: 彼女はおばあさんと住んでいる。
sentence_meaning: She lives with her grandmother.

mnemonic: 元 a person at their starting point and 気 the steam coming off them. Someone with their original energy still rising: げんき.
sentence: スミスさんのおばあさんは元気です。
sentence_meaning: Smith-san's grandmother is doing well.

mnemonic: いつ is when. Add も on the end and it stops being a question. Whenever you happen to ask, the answer comes back the same. Always: いつも.
sentence: 彼女はいつも元気だ。
sentence_meaning: She's always full of energy.

mnemonic: 扌 a hand next to 寺 a temple, the very same 寺 you met in 時間 and 待つ. This time the hand is closed around something and holding on: もつ.
sentence: 私は車を持っています。
sentence_meaning: I have a car.

mnemonic: Everybody, the whole lot of them, not one person left out. Ask whether anyone is missing and you get a flat "mean? nah" back: みんな.
sentence: 家族はみんな元気です。
sentence_meaning: Everyone in my family is doing well.

mnemonic: 亻 a person with 吏 an official standing over them: somebody put to work. Using a thing means exactly that. You put it to work: つかう.
notes: The verb. 用 よう is the noun and the suffix, things to do and made for.
sentence: 毎日、コンピューターを使います。
sentence_meaning: I use the computer every day.

mnemonic: 大 big, 丈 a full measure, 夫 a grown man. Three characters stacked up to say something is solid and there is nothing to worry about: だいじょうぶ.
sentence: 大丈夫ですか。
sentence_meaning: Are you alright?

mnemonic: 女 a woman at 台 a platform, taking the first step up onto it. Everything has to begin somewhere and this is that moment: はじめる.
notes: 始まる はじまる is it starting on its own. 始める is somebody starting it.
sentence: テストを始めてください。
sentence_meaning: Please start the test.

mnemonic: 今 this moment sealed off and 日 a day: this one day, the one you are standing in right now. Say kyo and it is already going: きょう.
sentence: 今日の勉強を始めましょう。
sentence_meaning: Let's begin today's studies.

mnemonic: 部 one section of something with 屋 a roof over the top of it. A walled-off piece of a house. Hey, ya, you knock before opening it: へや.
notes: A room with walls. 余裕 よゆう is room in the sense of spare capacity.
sentence: 部屋にキッチンがあります。
sentence_meaning: The room has a kitchen.

mnemonic: 亜 second-rate sitting on 心 a heart, pressing down on it. That is what bad feels like, and it will rule you if you let it: わるい.
sentence: あの人は悪い人です。
sentence_meaning: That person is a bad person.

mnemonic: The noise you make when a thing is fine but not actually good. A shrug, half a smile, and a long drawn-out maa: it'll do. まあ.
sentence: まあこれでいいだろう。
sentence_meaning: Well, this will do I suppose.

mnemonic: 食 is a lid sitting over a heaped dish. Lift it off, pick up the tab afterwards, and everything in between is eating: たべる.
notes: 食べる is the neutral word. 食う くう is the blunt, masculine one, and 召し上がる めしあがる is the polite one you use about a guest.
sentence: 昨日タイカレーを食べました。
sentence_meaning: I ate Thai curry yesterday.

mnemonic: 氵 water and 尺 a measure make a marsh, then 山 a whole mountain on top of it. Far more of the stuff than anyone needs: たくさん.
notes: Very often written in kana as たくさん. 多い おおい describes a noun as numerous, where 沢山 counts the amount. 十分 じゅうぶん is plenty as in enough.
sentence: 私には友達がたくさんいます。
sentence_meaning: I have a lot of friends.

mnemonic: 場 is 土 earth with the sun coming up over it, 所 is a 戸 door with an 斤 axe leaning by it. Two words for spot, stuck together: ばしょ.
notes: A location you could point to on a map. ところ is looser, and does grammatical work as well.
sentence: 行ってみたい場所がたくさんあります。
sentence_meaning: There are many places I want to go to.

mnemonic: 口 a mouth with 乎 the breath pushed right out of it. You shout across the restaurant for the waiter, yo, boo, over here: よぶ.
notes: The verb. 名前 なまえ is the name itself.
sentence: ウェイターを呼びましょう。
sentence_meaning: Let's call the waiter.

mnemonic: 重 something heavy with 力 power put behind it. That is what shifting a thing actually takes. Oo, go on, get it moving: うごく.
notes: Something moving under its own steam. 動かす うごかす is you moving it. 動き うごき is the movement itself.
sentence: エレベーターが動いています。
sentence_meaning: The elevator is moving.

mnemonic: 気 the steam coming off a person and 持 a hand holding on to it. Whatever you are carrying about inside you: key, mo, chi, きもち.
notes: How you feel about something. 感覚 かんかく is the sense itself, the faculty.
sentence: 彼の気持ちが分からない。
sentence_meaning: I don't understand his feelings.

mnemonic: 言 speech next to 隹 a small bird. A voice up in the trees you can hear but cannot place at all. Who on earth was that? だれ.
sentence: 誰と会ってみたいですか。
sentence_meaning: Who would you like to meet one day?

mnemonic: A swaddled infant with its arms out, drawn in three strokes. The same 子 you met inside 好き and 学校, now standing on its own: こ.
sentence: その子は日本語が分からない。
sentence_meaning: That kid doesn't understand Japanese.

mnemonic: ど- is the question, the same as always. どんな asks what sort of thing it is, not which one of them, but what type of thing: どんな.
sentence: スミスさんはどんな人ですか。
sentence_meaning: What kind of person is Smith-san?

mnemonic: 意 is 音 a sound over 心 a heart, 味 is 口 a mouth with 未 not-yet in it. The sense a thing carries before you can taste it: いみ.
sentence: 意味が分かりません。
sentence_meaning: I don't understand what you mean.

mnemonic: 言 speech and 葉 a leaf. Words come off a person the way leaves come off a tree. One at a time, and there is no end to them: ことば.
sentence: この言葉の意味が分かりません。
sentence_meaning: I don't understand the meaning of this word.

mnemonic: 心 a heart and 配 handing things out. Worry is your own heart being passed round to everybody else in the room. Shin-pai: しんぱい.
sentence: 母が心配しています。
sentence_meaning: My mother is worried.

mnemonic: 様 the way a thing looks and 子 a child. You glance across at somebody and read off how they are doing purely from the outside: ようす.
sentence: 彼女の様子を見てきます。
sentence_meaning: I'm going to see how she's doing.

mnemonic: 亻 a person and 言 their speech, stood side by side with nothing between them. Believing someone is exactly that: taking them at their word. しんじる.
sentence: 彼の言葉を信じています。
sentence_meaning: I believe his words.

mnemonic: 自 is a nose, and Japanese speakers point at their own to mean me. Add 分 a part and you have your own share of things: じぶん.
sentence: 分からない言葉は自分で調べてください。
sentence_meaning: Please look up any words you don't know on your own.

mnemonic: 言 speech going 周 all the way round a subject. Asking about it from every angle until the answer finally turns up. Shirabe: しらべる.
notes: Looking a thing up, in a book or online. 見上げる みあげる is raising your eyes.
sentence: 分からない言葉は自分で調べてください。
sentence_meaning: Please look up any words you don't know on your own.

mnemonic: A hand gripping a banner: an affair being conducted. Not an object you can pick up, a matter, a business, a thing that happens: こと.
notes: 物 is a thing you can hold; 事 is a thing that occurs.
sentence: インターネットで日本の事を調べました。
sentence_meaning: I researched things about Japan on the internet.

mnemonic: A frame with everything tucked up inside it, the whole lot under one cover. Oh, nudge them together, they match exactly: おなじ.
sentence: 私も同じこと考えてた。
sentence_meaning: I was thinking the same thing.

mnemonic: 申 to say humbly, 訳 a reason, ない none at all. You have no excuse left to offer for what you did, and you are saying so: もうしわけない.
notes: The formal apology, for work and for strangers. ごめん is what you say to a friend.
sentence: 彼には申し訳ないことをした。
sentence_meaning: I did something inexcusable to him.

mnemonic: Ask something with an obvious answer and this comes straight back at you. Of course we're going. It's a mochi run, no discussion: もちろん.
sentence: もちろん一緒に行きます。
sentence_meaning: Of course we'll go together.

mnemonic: Not a bit and not quite, all the way. Whatever adjective comes after it, とても takes it and turns the dial right up. Toe-tem-oh: とても.
notes: Plain very, with something positive after it. あまり does the negative half of that job, not very.
sentence: この本はとても面白い。
sentence_meaning: This book is very interesting.

mnemonic: 楽 was strings stretched across a wooden frame. Music, and the pleasure that comes with it. A tan, oh, she is enjoying herself: たのしい.
sentence: 彼はとても楽しい人です。
sentence_meaning: He's a very fun person.

meaning: pardon me, excuse me (e.g. when leaving)
mnemonic: 失 to lose and 礼 the bow you make at an altar. You are admitting you have dropped the manners, usually on your way out: しつれいします.
sentence: 失礼します。
sentence_meaning: Excuse me.

mnemonic: 手 a hand and 伝 passing something along. You put your own hand in and move the work on down the line for somebody else: てつだう.
notes: Lending a hand with a job. 助ける たすける is getting somebody out of trouble.
sentence: 私が手伝いましょう。
sentence_meaning: I will help you.

mnemonic: 忄 a heart next to 亡 lost: so busy that you have mislaid your own, and you have no time even to notice that it has gone: いそがしい.
sentence: 忙しいので手伝ってください。
sentence_meaning: I am busy so please help me.

mnemonic: 仕 a person serving and 事 a matter being conducted. Somebody doing whatever needs doing, all day long. She got a job: しごと.
sentence: 父の仕事を手伝います。
sentence_meaning: I help with my father's work.

mnemonic: 糸 thread running down the left-hand side, going on and on without a single break in it. That is what continuing looks like: つづける.
sentence: 仕事を続けてください。
sentence_meaning: Please continue your work.

mnemonic: 見る is you doing the seeing; 見せる is making somebody else do it. You hold the camera out and put it in front of their eyes: みせる.
notes: Holding a thing up for somebody to look at. 示す しめす is indicating or demonstrating it.
sentence: あのカメラを見せてください。
sentence_meaning: Please show me that camera.

mnemonic: The other reading of 家. Not the building this time but the people and the life going on inside it, your lot, your place: うち.
notes: Same kanji as いえ "house"; うち leans on the household rather than the structure.
sentence: うちへ帰ります。
sentence_meaning: I will go home.

mnemonic: 糸 thread inside 約 and 束 a bundle tied up tight. A promise is the two of you bound together by a thread you both agreed to: やくそく.
sentence: 友達と約束があります。
sentence_meaning: I have an appointment with my friend.

mnemonic: 亡 lost sitting on top of 心 a heart, the same 亡 you met in 忙しい. Something has gone from you and you cannot say when: わすれる.
sentence: 約束を忘れないでください。
sentence_meaning: Please don't forget your promise.

mnemonic: 宀 a roof with 寸 a hand held out underneath it. You put your hand over a thing and keep it that way. Your mother would: まもる.
sentence: 彼は約束を守る人です。
sentence_meaning: He's one to keep his promises.

mnemonic: The same かえる sound as 帰る "to go home", but a completely different kanji. This one turns a thing into something else: かえる.
notes: Careful: 帰る かえる is to return home. Same reading, different character.
sentence: 約束の時間を変えます。
sentence_meaning: I will change the time of the appointment.

mnemonic: Not yesterday and not this morning. The thing that happened a sec ago and is still hanging in the air right behind you: さっき.
sentence: さっきの話を続けましょう。
sentence_meaning: Let's continue the conversation we had earlier.

mnemonic: 今 this moment and 度 one turn of the wheel. Not this go round at all, but the very next one coming along after it. Con-doh: こんど.
notes: Written exactly like 今度 "this time". Whether it looks forward or at the thing in front of you decides which.
sentence: 今度はどこに行きたいですか。
sentence_meaning: Where do you want to go next time?

mnemonic: これ is this and から is from. From this point onward. You draw a line where you are standing and start counting there: これから.
sentence: これから考えます。
sentence_meaning: I will think about it from now.

mnemonic: 止 is a footprint planted flat on the ground: it goes no further. Pull the car in and leave it standing right there: とめる.
notes: Same characters as やめる, this reading stops a moving thing in a place. 止まる とまる is it coming to a stop on its own.
sentence: あのビルの前で止めてください。
sentence_meaning: Stop in front of that building, please.

mnemonic: The very same 止める, read やめる instead. This one halts an activity rather than a moving thing: quit talking, not park the car: やめる.
notes: Written identically to とめる, とめる stops a thing somewhere, やめる stops an action.
sentence: 話すのを止めてください。
sentence_meaning: Please stop talking.

mnemonic: 束 a bundle and 頁 a head, the same 頁 you met in お願いします. You hand the whole bundle of it over to somebody else to carry: たのむ.
notes: Asking somebody to do something. 聞く きく is asking a question.
sentence: 私はハンバーガーを頼みました。
sentence_meaning: I ordered a hamburger.

mnemonic: 言 speech with 午 noon standing beside it. Whatever was said first thing in the morning, by midday you have let it go: ゆるす.
sentence: 私は彼を許しました。
sentence_meaning: I forgave him.

mnemonic: 女 a woman with 喜 rejoicing stood right next to her. Not content and not fine, properly and visibly glad about the whole thing: うれしい.
sentence: 彼に会えて嬉しかった。
sentence_meaning: I was glad to be able to meet him.

meaning: to persevere, to do one's best
mnemonic: 頑 is 元 the start under 頁 a head: stubborn. 張 is 弓 a bow pulled 長 long. Head down, bowstring drawn, and keep going: がんばる.
sentence: 勉強もスポーツも頑張っています。
sentence_meaning: I do my best in sports and my studies.

mnemonic: The noise you make when a thing finally clicks into place. Not agreement exactly. The sound of the penny dropping: なるほど.
sentence: なるほど、よく分かりました。
sentence_meaning: I see, I understand quite well.

mnemonic: You have sat through all of it and now you are going to say the one sentence that was underneath the lot. So, basically: つまり.
sentence: つまり、あなたは何も知らないのですね。
sentence_meaning: So, basically, you don't know anything.

mnemonic: 囗 a border drawn the whole way round 玉 the jewel that is kept inside it. That is what a country is, on paper at least: くに.
sentence: どこの国が好きですか。
sentence_meaning: Which country do you like?

mnemonic: 亻 a person stood next to 憂 grief. Somebody who actually feels yours. Easy on you, and never once sharp about any of it: やさしい.
sentence: 彼はとても優しい人です。
sentence_meaning: He's a very kind person.

mnemonic: The same 嫌 you met in 嫌い, only shorter and blunter. Not a considered dislike at all, just no. Ee-yah, I would rather not: いや.
sentence: 私は待つのが嫌だ。
sentence_meaning: I dislike waiting.

mnemonic: そ- is your side of things, so そんなに means that much. The amount you have just suggested. Usually followed by a no: そんなに.
sentence: A「毎日忙しいですか。」B「そんなに忙しくないです。」
sentence_meaning: A: Are you busy every day?B: No, not that much.

mnemonic: 今 this moment and 回 one turn round the loop. This particular go of it, as opposed to any of the other ones. Con-kai: こんかい.
sentence: まあ今回は許してあげよう。
sentence_meaning: Well, I'll let you off this time.

mnemonic: A lid pulled right down over the day with the moon tucked in underneath it, and the whole place gone quiet. Yo-ru: よる.
sentence: 昨日の夜は家にいました。
sentence_meaning: I was at home last night.

mnemonic: 罒 a net thrown over 貝 a shell, and shells were the money once. You count them out into his hand and lead the cow away: かう.
sentence: 昨日、シーディーを買いました。
sentence_meaning: Yesterday, I bought a CD.

mnemonic: 今 now and まで as far as. Everything from back then right up to this exact second, and not a single step past it: いままで.
notes: Up to now, in time. これまで can also mean up to here, and tends to draw a line under what came before.
sentence: 今までどこにいたのですか。
sentence_meaning: Where have you been up until now?

mnemonic: 女 a woman and 又 a hand. The old sense was a servant, and it has stayed rude ever since. That bloke over there: やつ.
notes: Blunt to the point of insulting. Not a word to use about someone present.
sentence: 奴は人の言うことを聞かない。
sentence_meaning: That guy doesn't listen to what others tell him.

mnemonic: あ- is the far one, so あいつ is him over there. Same rudeness as 奴, just written in kana instead: あいつ.
sentence: あいつは本当にいい奴だ。
sentence_meaning: That guy is truly a great guy.

mnemonic: The word that opens a hypothetical. Everything after it has not happened, and most of the time it never will: もし.
sentence: もし時間があったら、ランチをしませんか。
sentence_meaning: If you have time, would you like to get lunch?

mnemonic: 理 the logic of a thing and 解 untying it with a blade. You take it apart until the sense falls out of it: りかい.
sentence: 理解してくれてありがとう。
sentence_meaning: Thank you for understanding.

mnemonic: 罒 an eye at 夕 evening, seeing something that is not in the room. You-me, and none of it actually there: ゆめ.
sentence: 私の夢は先生になることです。
sentence_meaning: My dream is to become a teacher.

mnemonic: 亻 a person, said bluntly. 俺 is the rough way a man says I, fine among mates, wrong almost everywhere else: おれ.
notes: Compare 僕, which is softer, and 私, which is safe anywhere.
sentence: 俺はロックを聞くのが好きだ。
sentence_meaning: I like to listen to rock music.

mnemonic: 隹 the small bird from 誰 again, this time impossible to get hold of. Muzukashii, and it will not sit still for you: むずかしい.
sentence: この本は難しいですね。
sentence_meaning: This book is difficult.

mnemonic: The same 今度 you already have for "next time". Pointed at the thing in front of you instead, it means this go: こんど.
notes: Identical to 今度 "next time". Whether it looks forward or at the present decides it.
sentence: 今度のテストはとても難しかった。
sentence_meaning: The test this time was really difficult.

mnemonic: Something is off and you cannot put your finger on it. Not funny-strange. The feeling that a thing does not add up: おかしい.
notes: Odd enough to be suspicious, and also funny. 変 is plain strange, 妙 is subtly off, 不思議 is strange and wonderful.
sentence: 彼の様子がおかしい。
sentence_meaning: He's acting strange.

mnemonic: 男 is 田 a field with 力 power put into it. A man at work. Add の子 on the end and you have the small version: おとこのこ.
sentence: 男の子たちがサッカーをしている。
sentence_meaning: The boys are playing soccer.

mnemonic: Built exactly like 男の子 with 女 woman in place of 男. The 子 child on the end is doing the same job: おんなのこ.
sentence: あの女の子を知っていますか。
sentence_meaning: Do you know that girl?

mnemonic: 宀 a roof over you with a bed underneath it. Lie down and that is the day finished with. Neh-ru: ねる.
notes: 宀 a roof and a bed. 寝る is going to bed and lying down; 眠る ねむる is actually being asleep. You can 寝る all night without much 眠る.
sentence: もう寝よう。
sentence_meaning: Let's sleep.

mnemonic: The same 伝 from 手伝う, passing a thing along the line. What you are passing this time is the message itself: つたえる.
sentence: みんなにこのことを伝えてください。
sentence_meaning: Please tell everyone about this matter.

mnemonic: Three short strokes with the middle one shortest of all. Chii-sai, and there is really not much of it there: ちいさい.
sentence: 私のカメラは小さいです。
sentence_meaning: My camera is small.

mnemonic: 辶 the road radical, you walk the length of the row and pick one out. Era-bu, and the rest stay where they are: えらぶ.
sentence: プレゼントを選ぶのはとても楽しいです。
sentence_meaning: Choosing presents is very fun.

mnemonic: 广 a shelter with people down on 土 the ground underneath it. Take the weight off and stay a while: すわる.
sentence: どうぞ座ってください。
sentence_meaning: Please sit down.

mnemonic: 簡 is 竹 bamboo around 間 the gap from 時間, 単 is one thing on its own. Nothing standing between you and the answer: かんたん.
notes: Easy to do. ただ means simply in the sense of merely.
sentence: このテストはとても簡単です。
sentence_meaning: This test is really simple.

mnemonic: The short form of お願いします. Same 原 plain, same bowed 頁 head. You are about to ask for something: おねがい.
sentence: お願いがあります。
sentence_meaning: I have a favor to ask.

mnemonic: 辶 the road with 隹 a bird on it, going the way birds go, forward, never backwards. Su-su-mu: すすむ.
sentence: 前に進んでください。
sentence_meaning: Please move forward.

mnemonic: 全 the whole lot under one roof, the same 全 from 全然. Not partly and not mostly, all of it: まったく.
sentence: 私には全く分かりません。
sentence_meaning: I don't understand at all.

mnemonic: The blunt question. Not how and not when. Why did that happen, and you would like an actual answer: なぜ.
sentence: なぜ来なかったの。
sentence_meaning: Why didn't you come?

mnemonic: 亻 a person again. 僕 meant "servant" once, which is why it lands softer than 俺, a boy, or a polite man: ぼく.
notes: Softer than 俺 and safer in most company, though still male. 私 わたし is the neutral one and always safe.
sentence: 僕は君が大好きです。
sentence_meaning: I love you.

mnemonic: A stream drawn with the current running straight down the middle of it. Meez, and it is out of the tap: みず.
sentence: 水を飲みます。
sentence_meaning: I drink water.

mnemonic: 食 eating with 欠 the same wide yawn that sits in 次 beside it. Same idea as eating, only there's nothing to chew. No-mu: のむ.
sentence: 水を飲みます。
sentence_meaning: I drink water.

mnemonic: 日 the sun with hours borrowed off it and nothing put in their place. He-ma, an afternoon with no plans in it: ひま.
notes: Free as in having the time. ただ is free of charge and 自由 じゆう is freedom.
sentence: 明日は暇です。
sentence_meaning: I am free tomorrow.

mnemonic: 日 the sun crossing the wall of 寺 the temple was the only clock they had. The monk nudges the dial round with his toe, key moment, とき.
notes: Same kanji as 時 じ 'o'clock'. とき is time in general and the 'when' of a sentence, じ only counts hours.
sentence: 暇な時は本を読んでいます。
sentence_meaning: In my free time, I read books.

mnemonic: The same sun-over-temple you met as とき, except this one never stands on its own. Put a number in front and it counts hours and nothing else. 三時: じ.
notes: Only ever follows a number: 3時 さんじ. Standing alone, the word for time is 時 とき.
sentence: A「何時ですか。」B「3時です。」
sentence_meaning: A: What time is it?B: It's 3 o'clock.

mnemonic: One stroke, and the first thing anyone ever writes. One itch, dead centre of your back, and nothing else in the world matters, itchy. いち.
notes: The reading shifts in compounds: 一つ ひとつ, 一日 ついたち.
sentence: 一から始めましょう。
sentence_meaning: Let's start from the beginning.

mnemonic: Two strokes stacked, a matching pair. You own exactly two of the thing that finds the coffee table leg in the dark, knee. に.
notes: Also read ふた- when counting things: 二つ ふたつ.
sentence: その人には二回会った。
sentence_meaning: I met that person twice.

mnemonic: Three strokes, and the last number you can read just by counting lines. Three guests at the door, and every one of them gets a さん after their name.
notes: Same sound as the honorific さん. The number sits in front of a counter, the honorific behind a name.
sentence: 彼女は三人の子供の母親だ。
sentence_meaning: She's the mother of three children.

mnemonic: Four walls with a pair of legs tucked inside them. Say よん. The other reading し is also the word for death, and nobody wants four of those.
notes: よん is the safe default. し survives in fixed compounds like 四月 しがつ, but is avoided elsewhere because it matches 死 death.
sentence: ハワイは四回目です。
sentence_meaning: This is my fourth trip to Hawaii.

mnemonic: The countdown starts at five fingers and folds them one at a time. The last one drops and so does the starter's flag: go. ご.
notes: Same sound as 語 ご 'language'. This one is the number.
sentence: 五人で旅行に行きました。
sentence_meaning: Five of us went on a trip.

mnemonic: A lid balanced on two thin legs. That's the whole shape. Six strings under your fingers, and the first chord lands: rock. ろく.
sentence: 彼には子供が六人います。
sentence_meaning: He has six children.

mnemonic: Take a 7 and tip it over backwards. Nana has seven of them on the mantelpiece, one china cat per grandchild: なな.
notes: なな is the safe default. しち holds on in 七月 しちがつ, but gets avoided otherwise because it's too easy to mishear as いち.
sentence: バナナが七本あります。
sentence_meaning: There are seven bananas.

mnemonic: Two strokes opening outward, wider the further down you look. Eight of them pour out of the hatch and every one is a bee: はち.
notes: はち is also the word for bee, written 蜂.
sentence: りんごを八個ください。
sentence_meaning: Please give me eight apples.

mnemonic: Nine people in the queue in front of you and not one of them has moved since you joined it. You're the tenth. きゅう.
notes: Read く in a few set phrases: 九月 くがつ, 九時 くじ.
sentence: 野球は九人で1チームです。
sentence_meaning: In baseball there are nine people on one team.

mnemonic: Two strokes crossing, every direction covered. The count is closed. Ten fingers come off the tally and wrap round one glass of juice: じゅう.
notes: Squeezes to じゅっ or じっ in front of counters: 十分 じゅっぷん.
sentence: その子は指で十数えました。
sentence_meaning: That child counted to ten on her fingers.

meaning: kun (usu. used with men younger or of the same age)
mnemonic: The same 君 you learned as きみ, but hung on the end of a name it goes soft. The teacher works down the register: Ken-kun, over here. くん.
notes: Written 君 but nearly always in kana. For boys, and for younger or junior men; さん is the safe choice for anyone else.
sentence: 健くんは１歳です。
sentence_meaning: Ken-kun is one year old.

mnemonic: Ink down a stranger's white sleeve, and nothing you can say makes it even again. That unsettled feeling is すみません. And it works for squeezing past someone too.
notes: Does double duty: an apology, and a way to get a stranger's attention. ごめんなさい is warmer and more personal.
sentence: すみません。今日は用事があります。
sentence_meaning: Sorry, I have something to do today.

mnemonic: Sleeves up, no ceremony. Who's doing the washing up? Yeah, all right. That shrug is やる, する with the polish taken off.
notes: Casual; する is the neutral one. やる also means to give, but only downward, to a junior, a pet, or a plant. 致す いたす is the humble form and 行う おこなう the formal one.
sentence: 一緒に宿題をやろう。
sentence_meaning: Let's do our homework together.

mnemonic: 彦 a fine young man and 頁 a head, the one worth putting on a poster. He catches it in the wing mirror of the car. Oh. So that is what they were all looking at: かお.
notes: The noun, the one on your head. 向く and 向かう are the verbs, facing a way.
sentence: 彼はタオルで顔を拭きました。
sentence_meaning: He wiped his face with a towel.

mnemonic: 今 now and 朝 morning welded together, and then read like neither of them. Sun up, moon still hanging there, and the case you packed last night still by the door: けさ.
notes: Irregular reading, けさ, never いまあさ.
sentence: 今朝は早く家を出ました。
sentence_meaning: I left the house early this morning.

mnemonic: 出 is one peak shoved up out of another. Steam leaves the kettle, you leave the house, the train leaves the platform, all of it でる.
notes: The thing leaves under its own steam. 出す だす is for putting something out.
sentence: 今朝は早く家を出ました。
sentence_meaning: I left the house early this morning.

mnemonic: The robot understands every word you say. そして, and then, without anyone asking for it, it dances. The word is the half-second before the thing that tops it.
sentence: このロボットは言葉が分かります。そして、ダンスも出来ます。
sentence_meaning: This robot understands words. On top of that, it can also dance.

mnemonic: The homework is on the table exactly where it was three hours ago. Not started, not moved. Your mum asks how it's going and まだ is the whole answer.
notes: With a negative it means 'not yet'; with a positive, 'still'.
sentence: 宿題はまだ終わっていません。
sentence_meaning: I haven't finished my homework yet.

mnemonic: You've had the menu long enough and the waiter's pen is already up. じゃ, that one. It's the sound of finally deciding.
notes: A casual squeeze of では. じゃあ is the same word held a beat longer. よく is the other well, meaning often or skilfully.
sentence: じゃ、それをください。
sentence_meaning: Okay, then I'll have that one.

mnemonic: A whole website with nothing on it for you, because every page of it was built for doctors. The lot tamed to one purpose: ため.
notes: Covers both the goal and the reason. 'for the sake of' and 'because of' are the same word.
sentence: これは医者のためのサイトです。
sentence_meaning: This is a website made for doctors.

mnemonic: 食 food with 反 a wrist turning it over in the pot, and a polite ご stuck on the front because rice has earned it. Go on, hand me a bowl: ごはん.
notes: Rice, and by extension the meal built round it: 朝ご飯 breakfast, 晩ご飯 dinner.
sentence: 私はパンよりご飯が好きだ。
sentence_meaning: I prefer rice to bread.

mnemonic: Not an address, just wherever someone happens to be. You slept at your friend's ところ, on the strip of floor between the sofa and the door.
notes: Stretches to time as well: 今のところ is 'at the moment'.
sentence: 私は友達のところに泊まった。
sentence_meaning: I stayed at my friend's place for the night.

mnemonic: 小 small, with one more stroke slicing another bit off the corner of it. Barely anything left in the glass, just a scooch: すこし.
notes: ちょっと is the casual version of the same idea.
sentence: 少し疲れました。
sentence_meaning: I'm a little tired.

mnemonic: 目 an eye up on 儿 legs, and it doesn't have to do a thing. You turn round and Fuji is already there above the rooftops, the whole of it: みえる.
notes: 見る みる is looking on purpose and 見せる みせる is showing someone. 見える is the thing simply being there to be seen.
sentence: ここから富士山がよく見えます。
sentence_meaning: You can see Mount Fuji well from here.

mnemonic: 辶 the road, and two sets of footprints leaving it in opposite directions. Your answer went one way and the marker's went the other: ちがう.
notes: Doubles as 'that's wrong'. Being different and being incorrect are the same verb, so it's also the everyday way to contradict someone.
sentence: 答えが違います。
sentence_meaning: That's the wrong answer.

mnemonic: 田 a field with 力 power driven into it, the one sent out to plough. He swings the thing round, catches his own toe with it and howls: おとこ.
notes: The everyday word. 男性 だんせい is the formal one, the box on a form.
sentence: 男の人が私たちに話しかけた。
sentence_meaning: A man began talking to us.

mnemonic: No gate, no honesty box, nobody taking money at the hot spring. You just walk in and get in. Ta-daa: ただ, and it costs you nothing.
notes: Same word as ただ 'simply'. This one is about price.
sentence: この温泉はただです。
sentence_meaning: This hot spring is free.

mnemonic: The same ただ as the free hot spring, thinned right down. You weren't after anything else. You ただ wanted to talk to her, and that was the whole of it.
notes: Same word as ただ 'free'. This one shrinks whatever follows it down to that and nothing more.
sentence: 私はただ彼女と話したかっただけです。
sentence_meaning: I just wanted to speak with her.

mnemonic: 人 a person and 間 the gap between people. Not the body. What goes on in the space between them, and it is a mess in there: にんげん.
notes: 人 reads にん here. The word means humankind as a species, or a person's character, never a headcount.
sentence: 人間の心は複雑です。
sentence_meaning: The human mind is a complex thing.

mnemonic: 亻 a person next to 乍, the old shape for notching wood. Breakfast doesn't turn up on its own, someone stood there and cut it into shape: つくる.
sentence: 今、朝ご飯を作っています。
sentence_meaning: I'm making breakfast now.

mnemonic: 咸 all of it landing on 心 the heart at once. Your knee goes and the whole of you knows about it before you've got a word for it: かんじる.
sentence: 膝に痛みを感じます。
sentence_meaning: I feel a pain in my knee.

mnemonic: A stroke sitting on top of the line, and that's the whole word. Head back, eyes up, the way you look when someone shouts down from a balcony: うえ.
notes: Same kanji as 上げる あげる 'to raise'. This one is the position, not the lifting.
sentence: 上を向いて。
sentence_meaning: Look up.

mnemonic: 弓 a bow hauled right back with 虫 an insect clinging on to it for dear life. That is what today's wind is doing to you on the way to the station: つよい.
sentence: 今日は風が強い。
sentence_meaning: The wind is strong today.

mnemonic: The same 出 you met as でる, except now there's a hand on it. The textbook is not leaving that bag by itself. He reaches in and drags it out: だす.
notes: 出る でる is the thing leaving under its own steam; 出す だす is somebody putting it out.
sentence: 彼はかばんから教科書を出した。
sentence_meaning: He took the textbook out of his bag.

mnemonic: 竹 bamboo 夭 bent double in the wind. That's the shape of the baby in the cot, and it's the shape of you about thirty seconds later: わらう.
notes: Covers laughing out loud and just smiling. One verb does both.
sentence: 赤ん坊が笑っています。
sentence_meaning: The baby is laughing.

mnemonic: 毎 every one of them and 月 the moon coming round again. It fills, the money goes in the tin, and then it fills again: まいつき.
notes: Also read まいげつ, but まいつき is the everyday one.
sentence: 私は毎月貯金をしています。
sentence_meaning: I save money every month.

mnemonic: 毎 every and 年 the harvest that only comes once. Same flight home, same December, until you've stopped counting them: まいとし.
notes: Also read まいねん. Both are common; まいとし is a touch more spoken.
sentence: 毎年、クリスマスに国へ帰ります。
sentence_meaning: I return to my country on Christmas of every year.

mnemonic: 夕 one evening with 夕 another stacked straight on top of it, and you can feel more behind that. Oh. Oh, there's a lot of them: おおく.
notes: The adjective is 多い おおい. 多く is the form that turns up in front of の for 'a lot of'.
sentence: 毎年多くの人が海外へ旅行する。
sentence_meaning: Each year, a lot of people travel abroad.

mnemonic: Seven hours. Or six and a half. It was dark and you weren't checking. くらい is the shrug you hang on the end of a number.
notes: ぐらい is the same word and just as common. Not 暗い くらい, which is dark.
sentence: 毎日、７時間くらい眠ります。
sentence_meaning: I sleep for about seven hours every day.

mnemonic: 女 a woman at 市 the market, already running the stall on her own while you were still small enough to be holding onto it: あね.
notes: Your own older sister. Someone else's is お姉さん. And you'd use that to her face, not あね.
sentence: 姉は大学生です。
sentence_meaning: My big sister is a college student.

mnemonic: Cord wound down a stake, one turn at a time, and he sits a turn below you. You hand him the present and he has it open before you've let go: おとうと.
notes: Your own younger brother. Someone else's is 弟さん.
sentence: 弟にプレゼントをあげました。
sentence_meaning: I gave a present to my younger brother.

mnemonic: 女 a woman and 未 not yet. She isn't one. She's off to primary school under a satchel bigger than she is: いもうと.
notes: Your own younger sister; someone else's is 妹さん. Shares its ending with 弟 おとうと.
sentence: 私の妹は小学生です。
sentence_meaning: My little sister goes to elementary school.

mnemonic: An arm bent hard at the elbow, the whole thing in one stroke. Your little sister lifts the end of the sofa you couldn't shift: ちから.
sentence: 私より妹の方が力があります。
sentence_meaning: My younger sister has more strength than I do.

mnemonic: 世 three tens joined at the foot, one generation, and 界 the lines drawn between 田 fields. Everyone alive, plus every border they argue about: せかい.
sentence: 世界の地図はありますか。
sentence_meaning: Do you have a map of the world?

mnemonic: 目 an eye fixed on 木 a tree, each taking the measure of the other, and 手 a hand out. Whoever is across the net from you, friend or not: あいて.
notes: Covers your doubles partner and the person you're playing against. The word only ever means 'the other side'.
sentence: 試合の相手は誰ですか。
sentence_meaning: Who is the opponent of the match?

mnemonic: 次 next sitting over 女 a woman. The shape of her a second before she turns. Right down the far end of the road you knew her by the outline alone: すがた.
notes: How a person looks, their figure. 形 かたち is the shape of a thing.
sentence: 遠くに彼女の姿が見えた。
sentence_meaning: Her figure was visible from a distance.

mnemonic: 歹 bare bones with a figure folded over beside them. The dog was ill a long while, and then the basket by the door was just a basket: しぬ.
notes: Blunt, and used plainly of animals. About a person, 亡くなる なくなる is the gentle way to say it.
sentence: 犬が病気で死にました。
sentence_meaning: My dog died due to sickness.

mnemonic: 日 the sun already up over one bare stalk, and nothing else in the day has started. Five in the morning, and the person you tell just says it back at you: はやい.
notes: Early on the clock. The same 早い also covers something taking little time, and 速い is the one for speed.
sentence: A「今朝、5時に起きました。」B「早いですね。」
sentence_meaning: A: I woke up at 5 A.M. this morning.B: That's early, isn't it?

mnemonic: The same 早い as five in the morning, pointed at a clock instead of a sunrise. Tokyo to Osaka before lunch, not quick feet, just not much time gone: はやい.
notes: Same word as 早い 'early'. Both are about the clock. Actual speed, a train or a runner, is 速い.
sentence: A「東京から大阪まで2時間半です。」B「早いですね。」
sentence_meaning: A: It takes two and a half hours from Tokyo to Osaka.B: That's fast, isn't it?

mnemonic: 豆 a bean balanced on 頁 a head. Which is about the size yours feels this morning. It's been going since you woke up: あたま.
notes: The head. 首 くび is the neck.
sentence: 今朝から頭が痛い。
sentence_meaning: My head has been hurting since this morning.

mnemonic: 戸 a door with 大 someone big coming back through it. You left the office an hour ago and here you are again: もどる.
notes: Going back to where you just were. 帰る かえる is going home, which is a different kind of return.
sentence: 今、会社に戻ります。
sentence_meaning: I'm going back to the office now.

mnemonic: Not since last year. Since before you could say why. The wanting never once stopped or started, it just sat there: ずっと.
notes: Also does comparisons, where it means 'by far'. ずっといい is much better.
sentence: ずっと日本へ留学したいと思っていました。
sentence_meaning: I always thought that I'd like to study abroad in Japan.

mnemonic: You come round the corner and she's crying, and you have no idea what happened. How did we get here, doing what: どうして.
notes: Softer than なぜ, which is the blunt written 'why'.
sentence: どうして泣いているの。
sentence_meaning: Why are you crying?

meaning: just as I thought, after all
mnemonic: Three weeks of telling everyone you'd settle down, and here you are pricing flights again. Yep. Knew it: やっぱり.
notes: やはり is the same word in a tie. Also does 'I've changed my mind back' at the front of a sentence.
sentence: やっぱり旅が大好きだ。
sentence_meaning: I really love to travel after all.

mnemonic: Tomorrow, definitely. Not today, obviously. Today there's still half a packet. つもり is what you've decided, sat at a safe distance from doing it.
sentence: 明日からタバコを止めるつもりです。
sentence_meaning: I intend to stop smoking starting tomorrow.

mnemonic: 必 a heart with a stroke driven clean through it, and 要 the waist everything else hangs off. Turn up without the book and the lesson falls apart: ひつよう.
sentence: これは授業に必要な本です。
sentence_meaning: This book is necessary for class.

mnemonic: 糸 a thread run all the way out to 冬 winter, the far end of the year. Four o'clock, the meeting stops, and there is no more thread: おわる.
notes: The thing ends by itself. 終える おえる is you finishing it.
sentence: 会議は4時に終わります。
sentence_meaning: The conference ends at four o'clock.

mnemonic: Not a name, not a job. Whoever it was that did the thing. You ring back and all you can offer is that you're the one who called earlier: もの.
notes: Same sound as 物 もの 'thing'. This one is always a person, and it's humble: you use it about yourself, not about a guest. 人 ひと is the neutral word and 方 かた the polite one.
sentence: 私は先ほど電話した者です。
sentence_meaning: I'm the person who called a while earlier.

mnemonic: 彳 the step radical with everything else trailing along behind it. Work first, and then, dragged along after it, the film: あと.
notes: Also read ご in compounds like 午後 ごご, and うしろ when it means physically behind.
sentence: 仕事の後、映画を見た。
sentence_meaning: I saw a movie after work.

mnemonic: こ- is the near one, same as これ. The receptionist doesn't point, she turns her whole hand over and lays it out flat: こちら, this way.
notes: The polite one. こっち is the same word, dropped into casual speech. Also a polite way to say 'this person' when introducing someone.
sentence: 受付はこちらです。
sentence_meaning: The reception desk is this way.

mnemonic: 向 a window set high in the wall, pointing one way and one way only. You've turned to face the office and you're already moving: むかう.
notes: Heading toward something. 向く むく is simply facing it, and 顔 かお is the noun.
sentence: 今、会社に向かっています。
sentence_meaning: I'm heading for the office right now.

mnemonic: Nobody has checked anything. But the sky is that colour, the washing is out, and you'd bet the house on it: きっと, it'll rain.
notes: Confidence, not proof. It goes with a guess you're sure about.
sentence: 明日はきっと雨が降ります。
sentence_meaning: It will surely rain tomorrow.

mnemonic: Nobody touched it. You're stood at the crossing and the red goes green on its own while you watch: かわる.
notes: The thing changes by itself; 変える かえる is you changing it. Careful with 帰る かえる, to go home. All three sit close together.
sentence: 信号が青に変わりました。
sentence_meaning: The traffic light turned green.

mnemonic: 冫 ice and 妻 a wife, the word started out meaning blood-chilling. It still means that much of a thing, only now it's the rain: すごい.
notes: Says 'a lot of', not 'good'. 凄い雨 is heavy rain, not lovely rain. Usually written in kana. 多い おおい is the plain a lot.
sentence: 凄い雨になった。
sentence_meaning: It began raining heavily.

mnemonic: A figure kneeling with her arms folded across, drawn in three strokes. The shape you've already met inside 好 and 姉 and 妹, on its own at last: おんな.
notes: Bare 女 can sound blunt about a person. 女の人 or 女性 じょせい is the safe way to say it.
sentence: 店員は若い女の人でした。
sentence_meaning: The salesclerk was a young woman.

mnemonic: Sitting down, at the table, plate cleared, nothing skipped. Not just eaten. Eaten ちゃんと, the way you were meant to.
notes: Casual, but not rude. It says the thing was done the proper way rather than half done.
sentence: 朝食はちゃんと食べましたか。
sentence_meaning: Did you properly eat breakfast?

mnemonic: 言 speech with one extra stroke shut inside the mouth. So it never becomes a word. Something big goes over outside and you never find out what: おと.
notes: A noise you hear. 声 こえ is a sound with a voice behind it.
sentence: 外で大きい音がします。
sentence_meaning: There is a loud noise outside.

mnemonic: 亻 a person and 本 the root they grow from. Not the mind, not the name, the thing that catches every cold going round: からだ.
sentence: 妹は体が弱いです。
sentence_meaning: My sister has a weak body.

mnemonic: 扌 a hand reaching up to a peg. The shirt goes over the hanger and stays there, holding its own weight: かける.
notes: Stretches a long way. 電話を掛ける is to make a phone call, 眼鏡を掛ける is to put glasses on. All of them hang something on something. 入れる いれる is putting a thing inside something.
sentence: 夫の服をハンガーに掛けた。
sentence_meaning: I put my husband's clothes on a hanger.

meaning: to walk, to go on foot
mnemonic: 止 one footprint planted flat with 少 a little more of the same behind it. Two prints, then a few, and that's the whole way to the station: あるく.
sentence: 駅まで歩きましょう。
sentence_meaning: Let's walk to the station.

mnemonic: 才 a sapling over 子 a child, then 才 a sapling in 土 the earth. Two ways of saying something is there at all. And the argument is about aliens: そんざい.
sentence: 宇宙人は存在すると思いますか。
sentence_meaning: Do you think that aliens exist?

mnemonic: 辶 the road, and you're already past the turning. Nobody stopped, and the afternoon went by the same way: すぎる.
notes: Hung on the end of another word it means too much of it: 高過ぎる is too expensive. 過ごす すごす is you spending the time rather than it passing you.
sentence: 時が過ぎるのは速い。
sentence_meaning: Time passes quickly.

mnemonic: 門 a gate with 耳 an ear at it, not listening for anything. Next door's telly comes through the wall whether you want it or not: きこえる.
notes: Built like 見える みえる. 聞く きく is listening on purpose, 聞こえる is the sound simply reaching you.
sentence: 隣の部屋からテレビの音が聞こえる。
sentence_meaning: I can hear the sound of the television from the next room.

mnemonic: One hand reaching down and another reaching up, with the thing passing between them. Your closest friend says it and you catch it full in the chest: うける.
notes: Stretches to anything you're on the receiving end of. 試験を受ける is to sit an exam, 手術を受ける is to have an operation.
sentence: 親友の言葉に、酷いショックを受けた。
sentence_meaning: I was terribly shocked at my friend's words.

mnemonic: 今 now and 年 the harvest, welded together and then read like neither of them. The one you're standing in, and this is the one you finally get to Italy: ことし.
notes: Irregular reading, ことし, never こんねん.
sentence: 今年はイタリアに旅行したい。
sentence_meaning: I want to travel to Italy this year.

mnemonic: 去 is 土 ground walked off with 厶 your own back turned to it, sat on 年 a year. France is done, the photos are on your phone: きょねん.
notes: 昨年 さくねん is the same thing in a formal register.
sentence: 私は去年フランスへ行った。
sentence_meaning: I went to France last year.

mnemonic: 来 the crop that hasn't come in yet, sitting on top of 年 a year. Nothing booked and nothing paid for, but next year, definitely, the two of you: らいねん.
sentence: 来年一緒に旅行しましょう。
sentence_meaning: Let's travel together next year.

mnemonic: 殳 on the right is a hand with a weapon raised in it. You can't bring yourself to do it even to the spider in the bath, glass, envelope, out the window: ころす.
sentence: 私は生き物を殺すのが嫌いだ。
sentence_meaning: I hate killing living things.

mnemonic: Someone tells you he did it, and your face moves before your mouth does. No. Not him. Surely not: まさか.
notes: Usually followed by a negative, or left hanging on its own as a flat 'no way'. 決して けっして is the flat never of a promise. まさか is disbelief.
sentence: まさか彼がやったんじゃないよね？
sentence_meaning: No way. He didn’t do that, did he?

mnemonic: 絶 a thread cut clean through and 対 a hand held up facing you. Nothing is getting past that one, not once, not ever, not a chance: ぜったい.
notes: Most often with a negative, for 'absolutely not'. 絶対に is the adverb form.
sentence: そんなことは絶対できないよ。
sentence_meaning: I can never ever do such a thing.

mnemonic: 理 the sense a thing makes and 由 the spot it came out of. You're forty minutes late and somebody would now like to know exactly where that came from: りゆう.
sentence: 遅れた理由を教えてください。
sentence_meaning: Please tell me why you were late.

mnemonic: A square drawn open and nothing inside it. The dentist wants it wider than that. Come on, all the way: くち.
notes: Turns into ぐち in compounds: 入口 いりぐち is an entrance.
sentence: 口を大きく開けてください。
sentence_meaning: Open wide, please.

mnemonic: 夕 an evening with 卜 a divining stick beside it. The readings were done out of doors, after dark. Step out there now and it hits you: そと.
notes: Reads がい in compounds. 外国 がいこく is a foreign country.
sentence: 外は暑いよ。
sentence_meaning: It's hot outside.

mnemonic: 辶 the road with 兆 the first sign of trouble showing on it. The window was open about two seconds and the bird was already gone: にげる.
sentence: 鳥が窓から逃げたよ。
sentence_meaning: The bird flew out of the window.

mnemonic: 誰 who, with か on the end so it stops being a question. Not anyone in particular. Just go and ask somebody, anybody: だれか.
notes: The same か turns 何 into 何か 'something' and どこ into どこか 'somewhere'.
sentence: 誰かに聞いてみてください。
sentence_meaning: Please try asking someone.

mnemonic: He is thirty-four years old and bouncing on the sofa. The whole way round, no part of him left out of it. He might as well be six: まるで.
notes: Nearly always has ようだ or みたい waiting later in the sentence.
sentence: 彼はまるで子供のようにはしゃいだよ。
sentence_meaning: He was excited just like a kid.

mnemonic: 亻 a person with 也 beside them. Somebody who isn't this one. You've been down every item on the list and there is nothing else left to try: ほか.
notes: Same kanji as 他 た. ほか is the everyday one, for other things, other ways, other places.
sentence: 他に方法がありません。
sentence_meaning: There's no other way.

mnemonic: The same 他 as ほか, stiffened up for a report. Asians mostly, and その他, the remaining thirty percent, filed away as everyone else: た.
notes: Same kanji as 他 ほか. た lives in set phrases like その他 and 他の, and mostly in writing.
sentence: 留学生はアジア人が多く、その他は3割です。
sentence_meaning: The majority of foreign students are Asian, with 30 percent from other regions.

mnemonic: 問 a 口 mouth at the 門 gate asking, and 題 a 頁 head with the thing set down in front of it. One of these has come up and it isn't going away: もんだい.
notes: Does both jobs. A problem you have, and a question on an exam paper.
sentence: 問題が一つあります。
sentence_meaning: There's one problem.

mnemonic: 今 now with 後 everything trailing along behind it. Not a date on a calendar, just all of it from here on. And you're asking to be looked after through the lot: こんご.
notes: 後 reads ご here, the same as in 午後 ごご. 今後ともよろしくお願いします is the standard line at the end of an introduction.
sentence: 今後ともよろしくお願いします。
sentence_meaning: I look forward to working with you in the future.

mnemonic: 普 everything lined up under one 日 sun, and 通 a road running straight through it. Food fine, service fine, nothing you'd tell anyone about: ふつう.
notes: On a train timetable it means the slow one that stops everywhere.
sentence: あの店は料理もサービスも普通です。
sentence_meaning: The food and the service at that restaurant is average.

mnemonic: The organ drawn with its chambers showing. Not his face and not what he says. What's actually in there, and it turns out to be honest: こころ.
notes: Covers heart and mind at once. Squeezes to しん inside compounds.
sentence: 彼は素直な心を持っている。
sentence_meaning: He has an honest heart.

mnemonic: Strokes tangled together over 日 the sun, the whole lot breaking open as it warms. Warm early this year, and everyone keeps saying so: はる.
sentence: 今年の春は暖かいね。
sentence_meaning: This year's spring is warm, isn't it?

mnemonic: A figure with an enormous head on it, drawn mid-dance. The season with all the festivals in it, and the one you'd take over the other three: なつ.
sentence: 私は夏が大好き。
sentence_meaning: I love summer.

mnemonic: 禾 grain next to 火 fire. The stubble burnt off once the harvest is in. She's picked that gap in the year to get married: あき.
notes: The season. 落ちる おちる is the verb, a thing dropping.
sentence: 彼女は秋に結婚します。
sentence_meaning: She'll get married this fall.

mnemonic: 夂 a pair of feet dragging, with 冫 two marks of ice sat underneath them. Canada in January, and nobody is getting anywhere quickly: ふゆ.
notes: The same 冬 that sits inside 終わる, the end of the year, and the end of things.
sentence: カナダの冬はとても寒いです。
sentence_meaning: Canadian winters are very cold.

mnemonic: 以 a marker put down to mean 'starting here', and 上 everything stacked above it. Thirty degrees and up, day after day, right through the summer: いじょう.
notes: Takes in the number itself, 30度以上 includes 30. 以下 いか does the same from below.
sentence: 夏は３０度以上の日が何日もあります。
sentence_meaning: There are several days in the summer that are 30 degrees Celsius or more.

mnemonic: Fever yesterday. それで, no school. The fever isn't just the thing that came first. It's the thing that kept you in bed: それで.
notes: そして only adds the next thing on. それで says the first thing caused the second. では is then as in well then, moving on.
sentence: 昨日は熱がありました。それで、学校を休みました。
sentence_meaning: I had a fever yesterday. Because of this, I took the day off from school.

mnemonic: 生 a shoot forcing its way up out of the ground. Not comfortable and not guaranteed, but a hundred years of it is the plan: いきる.
notes: 生 turns up everywhere with different readings. 生 なま is raw, 先生 せんせい is a teacher.
sentence: １００歳まで生きたいです。
sentence_meaning: I want to live to 100.

mnemonic: 最 a hand lifting the very top thing off the pile, and 初 the first cut of the knife into new cloth. Page five, right at the top of it: さいしょ.
sentence: 5ページの最初を見てください。
sentence_meaning: Please look at the beginning of page 5.

mnemonic: The same 最 reaching for the extreme end, except now it's 後, the one trailing at the back. Last day of the summer holiday, and you can feel it going: さいご.
notes: 後 reads ご here, same as in 今後 and 午後. 最初 さいしょ is the other end of the same pair.
sentence: 今日が夏休み最後の日だ。
sentence_meaning: Today's the last day of summer vacation.
