notes: Same word as 起こす "to wake up". 起きる おきる is a thing happening by itself; 起こす is somebody causing it.
sentence: 彼は暴力事件を起こしたんだよ。
sentence_meaning: He caused a violent incident.

mnemonic: The very same 起こす. What you are standing upright this time is a person, at six in the morning, against their considerable preference: おこす.
notes: Same word as 起こす "to cause". 起きる おきる is getting up yourself; 起こす is getting somebody else up.
sentence: 明日、6時に起こしてください。
sentence_meaning: Please wake me up tomorrow at six o'clock.

mnemonic: A pictograph drawn side on, and you have two of them. Say something across the room and she turns the good one towards you: me? me? みみ.
notes: 耳がいい is good hearing. 聞く きく is the listening you do with it.
sentence: 彼女は耳がよく聞こえません。
sentence_meaning: Her hearing isn't very good.

mnemonic: 生 the shoot pushing its way up, except this time nobody is doing it to anybody. The phone goes at four in the morning and there is a new person in the world: うまれる.
notes: 生む うむ is bearing the child; 生まれる is the child arriving. 生まれ うまれ on its own is where you are from.
sentence: 友達に子供が生まれました。
sentence_meaning: My friend had a baby.

mnemonic: 禾 grain being shifted about in 多 quantity, and 動 heavy things moved by force. Not a stroll. Getting an entire party and its luggage from one place to the next: いどう.
notes: 移動する is moving from place to place. 引っ越す ひっこす is moving house.
sentence: 私たちはレンタカーで移動しました。
sentence_meaning: We traveled around by a rental car.

mnemonic: 牙 a fang, 阝 a mound, and 魔 the demon out of 魔法 alongside. The suitcase is in the hall and everybody has to go round it. A jam, and somebody's fault: じゃま.
notes: 邪魔する is to get in the way. お邪魔します is said entering somebody's home, apologising for being the obstacle.
sentence: この大きい荷物はとても邪魔です。
sentence_meaning: This big luggage is a big hindrance.

mnemonic: 辶 a road with no destination attached to it. Nobody has told them what the game is and nobody needs to. Two hours in the park and not one plan between them: あそぶ.
notes: Covers playing and going out to enjoy yourself. 遊びに行く is going round to somebody's, not necessarily to play.
sentence: 子供たちが公園で遊んでいる。
sentence_meaning: The children are playing in the park.

mnemonic: 要 the part everything else hangs off, out of 必要. Walk in off the street with no booking and they seat you anyway. Whatever it was, it was not needed: いる.
notes: Same reading as いる, to exist, and usually written in kana, so context does the work. It takes が: お金が要る.
sentence: 予約は要りません。
sentence_meaning: Reservations are not required.

meaning: to be lost, to be used up
mnemonic: 無 the whole lot burnt away to nothing, with なる the turning into. It was there this morning. Where it went has stopped being the interesting question: なくなる.
notes: Used up or gone missing, both. Careful with 亡くなる なくなる, identical in speech, which is the polite word for somebody dying.
sentence: もうお金が無くなりました。
sentence_meaning: I've run out of money already.

mnemonic: 口 a mouth down at the bottom, which is why the word opens with くち. The visible edge of it, and hers are the part everybody comments on: くちびる.
notes: 口 くち is the mouth and 唇 くちびる begins with it. リップ is the loanword on the cosmetics.
sentence: 彼女の唇はとても可愛いです。
sentence_meaning: Her lips are really cute.

mnemonic: 着 the same character as arriving, because this is clothes arriving on you. Suit on at seven for a nine o'clock meeting, and it stays on until midnight: きる.
notes: Worn on the upper or whole body. 履く はく is anything below the waist. Same reading as 切る きる, to cut, which the kanji keeps apart. 入れる いれる is putting a thing inside something.
sentence: 今日はスーツを着ています。
sentence_meaning: I'm wearing a suit today.

mnemonic: 色 a colour, and 々 saying do that one again, so colours upon colours. He knows a bit about everything and intends to cover all of it: いろいろ.
notes: 々 means repeat the character before it, so this is 色色. It comes back six more times in this deck, in 人々, 我々, 日々, 少々, 元々 and 様々.
sentence: 彼は色々なことを知っている。
sentence_meaning: He knows about a lot of things.

mnemonic: He holds the door open with his back and waits. Nothing is said and nothing needs saying, because the whole invitation is in the eyebrows: どうぞ.
notes: Offers and invites: take it, go ahead, after you. どうも is thanks, and the two get muddled constantly.
sentence: こちらへどうぞ。
sentence_meaning: This way please.

mnemonic: 立つ standing and 上がる going up, welded together. He was sat down a second ago, the chair has scraped, and the whole table has stopped talking: たちあがる.
notes: Both halves are words you already have. It is also what a computer does when it boots.
sentence: 彼は急に立ち上がったの。
sentence_meaning: He suddenly stood up.

mnemonic: 田 a field sat on 心 a heart, and this is what stays up there rather than what you do about it. He asked her, and asking cost him everything he had: おもい.
notes: The thought or feeling itself, from 思う おもう. Later comes 重い おもい, heavy, which sounds identical.
sentence: 必死の思いで彼に頼んだよ。
sentence_meaning: I asked him out of desperation.

mnemonic: 以 the marker that fixes a boundary, and 前 everything in front of it. He lived here once, on the far side of that line, and the shop still remembers him: いぜん.
notes: Same 以 as 以上 and 以外. 以前 is before some point; 前 まえ on its own is simply ago.
sentence: 以前彼はこの町に住んでいたんだ。
sentence_meaning: He used to live in this town.

meaning: a little more, a bit more
mnemonic: もう pointed forwards, and 少し the scooch left in the glass. Not slower. A bit slower, and he is asking nicely because he stopped following two sentences ago: もうすこし.
notes: Both halves are already in the deck. もうちょっと is the casual version of the same request.
sentence: もう少しゆっくり話してください。
sentence_meaning: Please speak a little slower.

mnemonic: A dragon with 衣 clothing under it, arriving from above and giving nobody a say. The climbers heard nothing until it was already between them and the tents: おそう.
notes: Used of animals, weather and crime. 攻撃 こうげき is a deliberate assault, and more military.
sentence: 山で登山客が熊に襲われたよ。
sentence_meaning: Some climbers were attacked by a bear in the mountains.

meaning: to be found, to be caught
mnemonic: 見 an eye and 付 a hand fixing onto what it saw, the same as 見つける, except nobody is looking. The glasses turn up or they do not, and today they do not: みつかる.
notes: 見つける みつける is you finding it. 見つかる is it being found, or you being caught.
sentence: メガネが見つかりません。
sentence_meaning: I can't find my glasses.

mnemonic: A hand snatching down at a heart, the same 急 you have as きゅう. Fifteen minutes to cross town, and he is putting his coat on inside the lift: いそぐ.
notes: Same 急 as 急 きゅう, sudden. 急いで いそいで is quickly, said as an instruction.
sentence: 時間がないので、急いでください。
sentence_meaning: We don't have much time, so please hurry.

mnemonic: Two trains and a bus to get here, and now you are talking about leaving. Sit down. The effort is spent either way, so spend the afternoon too: せっかく.
notes: Marks effort already made that would otherwise go to waste. せっかくだから is since we are here anyway.
sentence: せっかく来たんだからゆっくりして行きなさい。
sentence_meaning: Since you've come all the way, why don't you stay for a while?

meaning: to get off, to go down
mnemonic: 阝 a mound, and somebody picking their way down off it. The bus is still moving and you are already at the door with a hand on the rail: おりる.
notes: Same reading as 下りる おりる. 降りる is getting off or out of something: a bus, a train, a car.
sentence: ここでバスを降ります。
sentence_meaning: I'm getting off the bus here.

meaning: to go down, to come down
mnemonic: The same おりる, written with 下, the mark that sits below the line. Not off anything. Simply down, one stair at a time, at the end of the corridor: おりる.
notes: Same reading as 降りる おりる. 下りる is going down stairs or a hill; 降りる is getting off a vehicle.
sentence: そこの階段を下りてください。
sentence_meaning: Please go down those stairs.

mnemonic: 刀 a blade on the right, and everything to its left is what the blade meets. Fold the paper, run a thumb down the crease, then take the scissors to it: きる.
notes: Same reading as 着る きる, to wear. Also switching off and cutting off: 電話を切る is hanging up. 傷 きず is the noun, the cut that is left.
sentence: この紙を半分に切ってください。
sentence_meaning: Please cut this paper in half.

mnemonic: 事 a matter being carried on, with 件 counting them off one at a time. Not a thing that happened. A thing that happened and now has a file with a number on it: じけん.
notes: An incident serious enough to be reported on. 事故 じこ is an accident.
sentence: その事件の犯人はまだ捕まっていない。
sentence_meaning: The perpetrator of that incident hasn't been caught yet.

mnemonic: 返 something turned round and sent back down the road, and 事 the matter itself. You sent it on Tuesday and there is still nothing in the box: へんじ.
notes: Same 返 as 返す かえす. 返事する is to reply, and 返事がない is the silence you get instead.
sentence: 友達からメールの返事が中々来ません。
sentence_meaning: My friend won't respond to my mail.

mnemonic: 酉 a wine jar, and everything too strong that ever came out of one. The review does not say the food was poor. It names the chef: ひどい.
notes: Usually written in kana. Covers awful and cruel both, from the weather to what somebody said to you.
sentence: 昨日のテストは酷い点でした。
sentence_meaning: I got a terrible score on yesterday's test.

mnemonic: The weight runs straight down the middle of the character and out the bottom. You get the case off the floor and regret every decision that led to it: おもい.
notes: Same sound as 思い おもい, a thought. Also does serious: 重い病気 おもいびょうき is a grave illness.
sentence: この荷物は重いですね。
sentence_meaning: This package is heavy.

mnemonic: 走 running with 己 yourself behind it, standing up out of nothing at all. Nobody caused this one and nobody is waking anybody: it simply happened. おこる.
notes: The 起 family: 起きる happens and also gets you up, 起こす causes it or wakes somebody, 起こる only ever happens. One vowel from 怒る おこる, to get angry.
sentence: この道ではよく事故が起こります。
sentence_meaning: There are many accidents on this road.

mnemonic: 辶 a road with a figure drawn upside down walking along it, against everything coming the other way. Whatever you assumed, the other way round: ぎゃく.
notes: 逆に means conversely, or on the contrary. As a noun it is the opposite of the thing.
sentence: 駅は逆方向です。
sentence_meaning: The station is in the opposite direction.

mnemonic: 糸 thread taking something in and stowing it, with 得 a hand coming back holding the prize. Not agreement. The point where the knot took and you stopped arguing: なっとく.
notes: 納得する is being satisfied by an explanation. 賛成 さんせい is agreeing with the proposal itself.
sentence: 彼の説明で納得できました。
sentence_meaning: I was able to accept his explanation.

mnemonic: The same 楽 as 楽しい, strings stretched across a wooden frame. Except this is not how it felt. This is what you did: sat down and took the whole afternoon: たのしむ.
notes: 楽しい たのしい is the feeling. 楽しむ is doing a thing for the pleasure of it.
sentence: 今日は一人の時間を楽しみたい。
sentence_meaning: Today I would like to enjoy some alone time.

meaning: to shout, to yell, to cry out
mnemonic: 口 a mouth with something twisted alongside it, and out it comes. Not aimed at anybody in particular, and the sake had a hand in it: さけぶ.
notes: 叫び声 さけびごえ is a scream. It is the noise rather than the message.
sentence: 彼女は助けを求めて大声で叫んだの。
sentence_meaning: She cried out for help.

mnemonic: 隹 a small bird on 木 a tree, then another, then the whole hedge is birds. Nobody organised it, nobody is in charge, and nobody is leaving: あつまる.
notes: 集める あつめる is you gathering them up. 集まる is them gathering by themselves.
sentence: 駅前に人が集まっています。
sentence_meaning: Lots of people are gathered in front of the station.

mnemonic: 木 timber put together into a frame, which is effort somebody chose to spend. Spend it on a person, or say 構わない and decline to: かまう.
notes: 構わない is the form you meet first: I do not mind, do not trouble yourself. Same 構 as 結構 けっこう.
sentence: 子供に構いすぎてはいけない。
sentence_meaning: You shouldn't give kids too much attention.

mnemonic: Three horizontal lines and one stroke joining them, and the man who claims to be the join. On his own, a king. Against another character, usually a jewel: おう.
notes: The same shape on the left of another character is normally 玉 jewel with its dot worn off, which is why 理 and 現 have jewels in them.
sentence: 王の墓を見学したよ。
sentence_meaning: I visited the royal grave.

mnemonic: 辶 a road with 余 whatever is left of it, and 中 the middle of that. Not arrived, not turned back. On the platform with the bag, chewing on another hour: とちゅう.
notes: 途中で is halfway through doing something. It covers distance and time both.
sentence: 途中で30分ほど休みましょう。
sentence_meaning: Let's take a rest on the way for about 30 minutes.

mnemonic: 忄 a heart with the same thing run through it again and again. The commute was unbearable in March and by June you are reading a book on it: なれる.
notes: に marks what you get used to: 仕事に慣れる. 慣れ なれ on its own is the habit.
sentence: 新しい家にはもう慣れましたか。
sentence_meaning: Have you gotten used to the new house yet?

mnemonic: 終わる stopped just short of being a verb. Not the ending. The point itself, the line drawn on the floor, and everybody already has their coat on: おわり.
notes: 終わる おわる is ending. 終わり is the end as a thing you can point at. 終える おえる is the verb.
sentence: 今月の終わりに国へ帰ります。
sentence_meaning: I will return to my country at the end of this month.

meaning: for the time being, more or less
mnemonic: 一 one and 応 a heart answering from under a shelter. One answer, given for now, with everything still unsaid sitting behind it: いちおう.
notes: Hedges whatever follows: more or less, for now, in principle. Often the speaker has reservations they are not going to state.
sentence: 彼にも一応知らせておいたほうがいいだろう。
sentence_meaning: It might be better to just let him know for now.

mnemonic: 弓 a bow, and the line beside it is the string coming back. Pull a card, pull a muscle, pull the door marked push: ひく.
notes: Very wide. Drawing a card, looking a word up, and 風邪を引く, catching a cold. Later comes 弾く ひく, playing a string instrument. 描く かく is the other draw, putting a picture on paper.
sentence: このドアは引いてください。
sentence_meaning: Please pull this door open.

mnemonic: 氵 water with 毎 every alongside it. Every drop there is, all in one place, and it does not stop at the horizon: うみ.
notes: 海 うみ is the sea. In compounds it reads かい: 海外 かいがい is overseas.
sentence: 海は広くて大きい。
sentence_meaning: The sea is vast and wide.

mnemonic: You put the pen down and say it to the room, and 言 is sat there on the left because this does not count until somebody has heard it: あきらめる.
notes: 諦めないで is do not give up. It is abandoning the attempt rather than losing.
sentence: 何でも簡単に諦めてはいけません。
sentence_meaning: You mustn't give up on everything so easily.

mnemonic: 必 the heart with something run right through the middle of it, same as in 必要. No exceptions, no discussion. It will happen and you arrange the rest around it: かならず.
notes: Stronger than きっと. 必ず is a guarantee; きっと is confidence.
sentence: 必ずシートベルトを着けてください。
sentence_meaning: Always wear your seat belt.

mnemonic: 犭 a beast flattened into the grass, and every part of it pointed at one thing out in the field. It decided some time ago: ねらう.
notes: Aiming a weapon, and equally going after a job or a prize.
sentence: 来年は優勝を狙います。
sentence_meaning: We will aim for a victory next year.

mnemonic: The tag has been turned over twice and there is still no number on it. Somebody is going to have to ask, and the somebody is you: いくら.
notes: いくらですか is how much is it. いくら〜ても is a different pattern altogether, meaning no matter how much.
sentence: この靴はいくらですか。
sentence_meaning: How much are these shoes?

mnemonic: 艹 grass and 氵 water on their way down, the same as 落ちる, except this time a hand let go. Phone, step, pavement: oh, toss. おとす.
notes: 落ちる おちる is it falling. 落とす is you dropping it, and it also covers losing something.
sentence: 道でスマホを落としました。
sentence_meaning: I dropped my smartphone on the street.

mnemonic: 部 one section of a thing with 分 a blade splitting it, so a part of a part. Not the whole essay. The paragraph somebody has underlined twice: ぶぶん.
notes: 全部 ぜんぶ is all of it; 部分 is a portion of it.
sentence: この部分は問題ないです。
sentence_meaning: There's no problem with this part.

mnemonic: 必 a heart with a stroke through it and 死 bare bones alongside. Certain death, used as an adverb. He asked the way you ask when there is no second go: ひっし.
notes: 必死に is desperately or frantically. Literally certain death, which is about the tone of it.
sentence: 学生たちは授業についていくのに必死です。
sentence_meaning: Students are desperately trying to follow the class.

mnemonic: That 王 is the jewel one, not the king, the same as it is in 理. Snow in May, and every person on the street has stopped with a phone up: めずらしい.
notes: Also does unusual for you, as a compliment or a dig: 珍しいね, you are never normally here.
sentence: こんな大きなダイヤは珍しいです。
sentence_meaning: A diamond big like this is rare.

mnemonic: 意 a sound landing on 心 a heart, and 外 everything outside. What happened was outside the part your mind had set aside room for: いがい.
notes: Same reading as 以外 いがい, except for. 意外 is a surprise, 以外 is an exclusion, and only the kanji separates them.
sentence: 意外にも彼は独身です。
sentence_meaning: Surprisingly, he is single.

mnemonic: 報 a hand passing the news along, and 告 牛 a cow announced by 口 a mouth. Not the news. The written version somebody has to sign at the bottom: ほうこく.
notes: 報告する is to report. Same 報 as 情報 じょうほう.
sentence: 昨日の会議について報告があります。
sentence_meaning: There's a report about yesterday's conference.

mnemonic: 扌 a hand on the left, closing and not opening again. The same grip that shapes a nigiri, rice pressed into form by the fist alone: にぎる.
notes: 握手 あくしゅ is a handshake, and おにぎり the rice ball comes from this verb.
sentence: 少女は母親の手を握った。
sentence_meaning: The girl clasped her mother's hand.

mnemonic: 糸 a thread pulled into 吉 a lucky knot, and 婚 a woman at dusk, which is when it was done. The knot is the whole idea, and every language has it: けっこん.
notes: 結婚する is to get married. Same 結 as 結果 けっか and 結構 けっこう.
sentence: 来月、姉が結婚します。
sentence_meaning: My older sister is getting married next month.

mnemonic: 戦う stopped just short of being a verb. Not the fighting. The thing itself, with a name and a date and a field somebody can point at: たたかい.
notes: 戦う たたかう is to fight. 戦い is the fight as a noun, and 戦争 せんそう is a war.
sentence: 長い戦いが終わった。
sentence_meaning: The long battle came to an end.

mnemonic: 咸 all of it landing on 心 a heart, and 謝 words loosed like an arrow. Not thanks said on the way out of the door. The kind you sit down and write: かんしゃ.
notes: 感謝する is to be grateful. ありがとう is the everyday version.
sentence: 友達にいつも感謝しています。
sentence_meaning: I am always thankful to my friends.

mnemonic: 氵 water thrown hard at something rather than running past it. The argument did not build up to anything. It arrived at that volume and stayed there: はげしい.
notes: Rain, arguments, exercise, competition. Anything carrying more force than it needs.
sentence: 激しい雨が降っています。
sentence_meaning: A very heavy rain is falling.

mnemonic: 亻 a person arriving on the floor, and this time nobody put them there. He was fine at the table and then he was not, and the chair went with him: たおれる.
notes: 倒す たおす is you knocking it down. 倒れる is it going over, and of a person it means collapsing.
sentence: 地震で家が倒れました。
sentence_meaning: The house collapsed from the earthquake.

mnemonic: A figure already turning away from the bowl, done with it. Whatever you were about to suggest has happened, and there is nothing left to decide: すでに.
notes: Written and formal. もう is the everyday already.
sentence: そのことは既にみんな知っています。
sentence_meaning: Everyone already knows that.

mnemonic: 疒 the sickness radical wrapped round 皮 skin. Not ill. Worn through to the outside layer, and the stairs have opinions about it now: つかれる.
notes: お疲れ様 おつかれさま is said to somebody who has been working, and it is nearer to well done than to you look tired.
sentence: 私は疲れてふらふらです。
sentence_meaning: I'm tired and feel dizzy.

mnemonic: 生 a shoot pushing up, and 活 氵 water with 舌 a tongue in it, both of them alive. Not being alive. How you go about it, day after day: せいかつ.
notes: 命 いのち is life itself; 生活 is how it gets lived. 生活費 せいかつひ is living costs.
sentence: 日本の生活は大変ですが、とても楽しいです。
sentence_meaning: Life in Japan is hard but also really fun.

mnemonic: 土 earth with the sun coming up over it, the same 場 as 場所. On its own it thins out: not the address, the occasion, and the room it happened in: ば.
notes: 場所 ばしょ is the physical place. 場 alone leans towards the occasion: その場で, on the spot. ところ is the loose everyday place.
sentence: この場でお礼を言わせてください。
sentence_meaning: Please let me take this opportunity to offer my gratitude.

mnemonic: 愛 a heart carried about in the middle of the character, with する bolted on to make it a thing you do. Not a feeling you have. A thing you keep choosing: あいする.
notes: Heavier and far more written than 好き. 愛 あい on its own is love as a noun.
sentence: 私は家族を愛しています。
sentence_meaning: I love my family.

mnemonic: 冫 the ice marks again, and whatever they touch goes the same way. The tap runs and your hand is off it before you decided to move: つめたい.
notes: Cold to the touch, and also cold in manner. 寒い さむい is cold weather.
sentence: 冷たいジュースが飲みたいです。
sentence_meaning: I want to drink cold juice.

mnemonic: 扌 a hand on the left, opening. Everything else in the character is what it was holding until a second ago: すてる.
notes: 捨てる is discarding on purpose. 落とす おとす is dropping by accident, which is the difference that matters.
sentence: この野菜は捨てないでください。
sentence_meaning: Please don't throw these vegetables away.

mnemonic: 辶 the road, and where 過ぎる is time going past you, this is you doing something with it. A whole Sunday, and you chose every hour of it: すごす.
notes: 過ぎる すぎる is time passing. 過ごす is you passing it, deliberately.
sentence: 暖かい国でゆっくり過ごしたいです。
sentence_meaning: I want to spend my time living leisurely in a warm country.

mnemonic: 食 a lid over a heaped dish and 事 a matter being conducted. Not the food. The event: everybody sat down at once with the phones face down: しょくじ.
notes: 食事する is to have a meal. ご飯 ごはん is the everyday word for it.
sentence: 来週みんなで食事しましょう。
sentence_meaning: Let's have a meal with everyone next week.

mnemonic: 亻 a person with 動 movement bolted onto them, which is the whole of the idea. Coat on the hook, hat on the rack, and eight hours of it: はたらく.
notes: 仕事 しごと is the job. 働く is the doing of it. 働き者 はたらきもの is a hard worker.
sentence: 姉は銀行で働いています。
sentence_meaning: My big sister works at a bank.

mnemonic: 竹 bamboo strips with 合 the matching half fitted against them, and this is the half that fits rather than the fitting of it. It was on the board all along: こたえ.
notes: 答える こたえる is answering. 答え is the answer itself.
sentence: 答えが分かりません。
sentence_meaning: I don't know the answer.

mnemonic: The frame is the gust, and 虫 the insect inside it is what the old idea reckoned the wind was carrying. It comes round the building and takes your hat: かぜ.
notes: 風邪 かぜ, with a different second character, is a cold. 風邪を引く かぜをひく is catching one.
sentence: 今日は風が強いです。
sentence_meaning: The wind is strong today.

mnemonic: Soot in the window with 灬 fire underneath, which is where soot comes from. The crow on the fence is that colour all over, beak included: くろい.
notes: 黒 くろ is the colour as a noun. Same 黒 as 黙る だまる, where it sits over a dog. 暗い くらい is dark as in no light rather than the colour.
sentence: 彼女は黒いドレスを着ています。
sentence_meaning: She's wearing a black dress.

mnemonic: 力 power on the right, an extra shoulder under the load, the same as 助ける. Except this time it is your load and somebody else's shoulder: たすかる.
notes: 助ける たすける is you helping. 助かる is being helped, and 助かった is what you say when it works out.
sentence: 彼はシートベルトをしていたので助かったんだ。
sentence_meaning: He survived because he was wearing a seat belt.

meaning: to receive, to take (someone's words or behavior)
mnemonic: 受ける taking what comes and 取る closing a hand round it, welded together. Not simply that it arrived. You have it, and you have signed for it: うけとる.
notes: Both halves are already in the deck. It also covers taking a remark a certain way: 悪く受け取る. 頂く いただく is the humble receive, and かかる is take of time or money.
sentence: 彼からメールを受け取りました。
sentence_meaning: I got an email from him.

meaning: to be enough, to be sufficient
mnemonic: 口 a knee over the foot below it, the same 足 as your leg. Here it is about reach: whether what you have gets you as far as the line. It does not: たりる.
notes: 足りない is the form you meet more often, meaning not enough. 十分 じゅうぶん is having plenty.
sentence: お金がちょっと足りません。
sentence_meaning: There's not quite enough money.

mnemonic: 刂 a blade telling two things apart, and 断 an axe taking one of them off for good. Both halves are somebody deciding, and neither of them is reversible: はんだん.
notes: 判断する is to judge or to decide. 決める きめる is picking; 判断 is the weighing that comes first.
sentence: 彼の判断は正しい。
sentence_meaning: His judgment is correct.

mnemonic: 未 a tree with the top branch not out yet, and 来 the crop that has not come in. Nothing here has happened, which is the entire point of it: みらい.
notes: 未 means not yet, and turns up in 未定 みてい, undecided. 将来 しょうらい is your own future rather than the world's.
sentence: 未来は誰にも分からない。
sentence_meaning: Nobody knows the future.

mnemonic: The same 食 as 食べる, a lid over a heaped dish, except nobody here is being delicate about it. He eats standing up over the sink: くう.
notes: Blunt and masculine. 食べる たべる is the neutral one. 食う also does living on something: 芸で食う.
sentence: 腹一杯食った。
sentence_meaning: I ate heartily.

mnemonic: 八 splitting with 刀 a blade, so a portion cut off the whole. Your share of the bill, your share of the work, and the bun that comes with it: ぶん.
notes: The portion belonging to something. 自分 じぶん is your own share, which is where the word for self comes from.
sentence: このケーキはあなたの分です。
sentence_meaning: This cake is your portion.

mnemonic: そ- is your side of things again, and this is the offhand way of pointing at it. Not over there. Where you are, and nobody is reaching for こちら: そっち.
notes: The casual form of そちら. こっち, そっち, あっち, どっち run exactly as これ, それ, あれ, どれ do.
sentence: そっちが私の部屋です。
sentence_meaning: That's my room over there.

mnemonic: 上 above the line and 手 a hand, so a hand above everybody else's. He makes it look like nothing at all, and you may as well not have tried: うまい.
notes: Also means tasty. 上手 じょうず is the same two characters read differently, and is the politer word for skilled.
sentence: 彼はサッカーも野球もとても上手いです。
sentence_meaning: He's good at soccer and baseball.

mnemonic: 𠆢 a lid coming down onto 口 a mouth, the same as 合う, except this time somebody is doing the fitting. Watches set to the same minute before anyone leaves: あわせる.
notes: 合う あう is things matching by themselves. 合わせる is you making them match.
sentence: 日時はご都合に合わせます。
sentence_meaning: The date can be scheduled according to your circumstances.

mnemonic: 大 big and 切 a blade, which reads wrong until you think of cutting a thing out in order to keep it. Tie it, set it aside, let nobody else near: たいせつ.
notes: 大事 だいじ is the near twin and either does most of the time. 大切にする is to treasure something.
sentence: これは母が大切にしていた指輪です。
sentence_meaning: This is a ring that meant a lot to my mother.

mnemonic: 艹 grass on top, and underneath it something caught halfway through turning. One stem in a jar and the whole room is different: はな.
notes: Later comes 鼻 はな, nose, which sounds identical. 花見 はなみ is flower viewing.
sentence: 母は花が好きです。
sentence_meaning: My mother likes flowers.

mnemonic: 言 speech with an arrow loosed beside it, the same 謝 as 感謝. Words sent out on purpose, except this time sending them costs you something: あやまる.
notes: Same 謝 as 感謝 かんしゃ. Both are words you have to actually put out there.
sentence: 自分が悪い時は謝りましょう。
sentence_meaning: Be sure to apologize when you've done something wrong.

meaning: to snatch, to take by force
mnemonic: The bird was in somebody else's hand a moment ago, and the big figure standing over it did not ask. It is his now: うばう.
notes: Taking by force. 取る とる is neutral, and 盗む ぬすむ is stealing quietly.
sentence: その男は彼女のバッグを奪ったぞ。
sentence_meaning: That man stole her bag.

mnemonic: 力 power at the bottom and everything above it stacking up. Once it is moving nobody needs to push any more, and nobody could stop it either: いきおい.
notes: 勢いで means on a roll, carried by it. 力 ちから is strength standing still.
sentence: そのチームには勢いがありますね。
sentence_meaning: That team has momentum.

mnemonic: 氵 water with 戻 returning beside it, because it comes back whether you want it to or not. She got through the whole speech and then the last line went: なみだ.
notes: 涙が出る なみだがでる is the usual way of saying you are crying. 泣く なく is the act itself.
sentence: 動物の映画を見て、涙が出ました。
sentence_meaning: I saw a movie about animals and cried.

mnemonic: 雨 rain split into 分 parts, 囲 a border drawn round it, and 気 the steam of the place. Three characters for a thing nobody can point at. It was fun, then it went icky: ふんいき.
notes: The feel of a place or a moment. 空気 くうき does the same job in 空気を読む, reading the room.
sentence: とても雰囲気のいいお店ですね。
sentence_meaning: The shop has a really good atmosphere.

mnemonic: 口 a mouth on the left with nothing whatsoever beside it. Sound coming out with no substance behind it, which is the whole definition: うそ.
notes: 嘘つき うそつき is a liar. 嘘! on its own is you are kidding.
sentence: 嘘じゃありません。本当です。
sentence_meaning: It's not a lie. It's true.

mnemonic: 月 the moon down in the corner, and the whole rest of the character is the distance to it. Wanting a thing you cannot reach from here, and no amount of zoom helps: のぞむ.
notes: 希望 きぼう is hope as a noun. 望む is the wanting itself.
sentence: 彼は私との結婚を望んでいます。
sentence_meaning: He hopes to marry me.

mnemonic: 糸 thread pulled until it will not give, and 張 a bow drawn 長 long. Two things at full stretch. Stood up to speak and your voice has gone elsewhere: きんちょう.
notes: 緊張する is to be nervous. Same 張 as 頑張る がんばる, where the stretch is effort rather than nerves.
sentence: 昨日のスピーチはとても緊張しました。
sentence_meaning: I was really nervous during my speech yesterday.

mnemonic: 一 one and 緒 a thread with a person on the end of it. Two of you tied into a single strand, going the same way whether or not it was agreed: いっしょ.
notes: 一緒に is together as an adverb. It also means the same: 一緒だ, they are identical.
sentence: 一緒に食事しよっか。
sentence_meaning: Do you want to eat together?

mnemonic: 求 seeking with 攵 a hand striking alongside, so going in and getting somebody out. Straight off the bank and scooped the dog up with one arm: すくう.
notes: 助ける たすける is helping, up to and including rescue. 救う is the rescue itself, and heavier.
sentence: 彼女は通りがかりの人に救われたよ。
sentence_meaning: She was saved by a passing stranger.

mnemonic: 自 the nose you point at to mean me, the same as in 自分. Except this one is an adverb: nobody asked him, nobody sent him, he went: みずから.
notes: Formal and written. 自分で じぶんで is the everyday by myself.
sentence: 社長自らがその会社と交渉したよ。
sentence_meaning: The president himself negotiated with that company.

mnemonic: 土 earth on the left and 面 the face of a thing. Not the soil and not the planet. The flat top of it, which is what you land on: じめん.
notes: 地 reads ち on its own meaning ground, and じ in compounds like this one.
sentence: 地面に何か絵が描いてあるぞ。
sentence_meaning: There is some kind of picture drawn on the ground.

mnemonic: 失 a hand letting go without meaning to, and 敗 money with a hand striking at it. You lost hold and it cost something, and everybody saw: しっぱい.
notes: 失敗する is to fail or to make a mistake. 成功 せいこう is succeeding.
sentence: 一度の失敗であきらめてはいけないよ。
sentence_meaning: You must not give up after one blunder.

mnemonic: 辶 the road again, except this one takes the long way on purpose. He saw them at the far end of the aisle and found something urgent in the other direction: さける.
notes: Avoiding a thing or a person. 逃げる にげる is running once it has already started.
sentence: 彼女は昨日から私のことを避けているようなんだ。
sentence_meaning: She seems to have been avoiding me since yesterday.

mnemonic: 穴 an opening cut into the wall with 心 a heart sat below it, which is about right. Nothing whatsoever to see out there, and you look anyway: まど.
notes: 窓口 まどぐち is a service counter, the window you queue at.
sentence: 窓を開けてください。
sentence_meaning: Please open the window.

mnemonic: 素 undyed thread with nothing done to it, and 直 an eye looking dead ahead. No angle, no colour added. She says what she thinks and it costs her nothing: すなお.
notes: Not the same as 正直 しょうじき. 正直 is not lying; 素直 is not being difficult, and it is a compliment about temperament.
sentence: 彼女はとても素直で可愛いですね。
sentence_meaning: She is very honest and cute.

mnemonic: A pictograph of a cut with the grain drawn through it. Nick a slice off the joint before it reaches the table and see what happens: にく.
notes: The same 肉 sits inside 月 when 月 carries the flesh sense, which is why 胸 and 腕 have it.
sentence: 肉が焼けました。
sentence_meaning: The meat is cooked.

mnemonic: 冗 somebody under a roof with nothing to do, and 談 talk warming up next to a double fire. Joe and Dan have been at it an hour and none of it was true: じょうだん.
notes: 冗談でしょ is you are joking. 嘘 うそ is a lie meant to deceive; a 冗談 is not.
sentence: 冗談は止めてください。
sentence_meaning: Please stop joking.

mnemonic: 余 whatever did not get used, and 裕 clothing cut as wide as a valley. Room to move about inside it. He finished with an hour spare and never hurried: よゆう.
notes: Time, money or composure, all the same word. 余裕がある is having slack in the system. 部屋 へや is the other room, the one with walls.
sentence: 出発まで時間の余裕があります。
sentence_meaning: We have some time until departure.

mnemonic: 連 carts strung out along a road, and 絡 thread tying one to the next. Not a conversation. The wire staying up between you: れんらく.
notes: 連絡する is to get in touch. 連絡先 れんらくさき is your contact details.
sentence: 仕事が終わったら連絡します。
sentence_meaning: I'll contact you when I finish the job.

mnemonic: 人 a person and 生 the shoot pushing up. Not being alive, which is 命, and not daily living, which is 生活. The whole span, looked at from the far end: じんせい.
notes: 命 いのち is life itself, 生活 せいかつ is how it gets lived, 人生 is the course of one.
sentence: 彼は自分の人生を振り返ったわ。
sentence_meaning: He looked back on his life.

meaning: to emit, to set free, to shoot (e.g. an arrow or bullet)
mnemonic: 方 a direction with 攵 a strike behind it. Point the thing and let go of it. An arrow, a bird, or the smell off something left in the sun: はなつ.
notes: 放す はなす is letting go, and 放送 ほうそう is broadcasting, the same idea aimed outward.
sentence: 的に向けて矢を放った。
sentence_meaning: I shot the arrow at the target.

mnemonic: 氵 water, asking nobody's permission about anything at all. The tap and the Niagara are doing the same thing at different volumes: ながれる.
notes: Time, water, music and rumours all 流れる. 流す ながす is you making it flow.
sentence: ラジオから美しい音楽が流れています。
sentence_meaning: Beautiful music is coming from the radio.

mnemonic: 牛 the cow walked in through the temple gate, and 刂 the blade that cuts one thing out of the pile. Both halves single something out, so twice over it must be: とくべつ.
notes: Same 特 as 特に とくに and the same 別 as 別 べつ. Both are about picking one out of the rest.
sentence: あなたは私にとって特別な人です。
sentence_meaning: You're special to me.

mnemonic: 連 carts strung along a road again, and 中 the middle of them. That lot, taken as a single thing, and not admiringly: れんちゅう.
notes: Familiar or dismissive depending entirely on tone. Not a word for people you are being polite about.
sentence: あの連中は本当に面白い。
sentence_meaning: That bunch is really interesting.

mnemonic: 両 two of a thing inside one frame, and 手 a hand. Both of them at once, because whatever it is will not go in one: りょうて.
notes: 両 means both: 両親 りょうしん is parents and 両方 りょうほう is both sides.
sentence: 彼は両手を握り締めたの。
sentence_meaning: He clenched both his fists.

mnemonic: 土 earth piled up, and then piled up again. Nobody added any of them on purpose. You open the drawer and there are eleven where there were four: ふえる.
notes: 増やす ふやす is you increasing it. 減る へる is the opposite.
sentence: この町は人口が増えた。
sentence_meaning: The population has increased in this town.

meaning: to meet (by chance), to come across
mnemonic: 出 coming out and 会う meeting, welded together. Neither of you arranged any of it. You came round the corner and there they were, eight years later: であう.
notes: 会う あう is meeting, arranged or not. 出会う is specifically running into somebody.
sentence: アメリカで彼女と出会いました。
sentence_meaning: I met her in the United States.

mnemonic: 少 a small quantity of 年 years, which is all a boy is. The word turns up on the news and in manga titles and almost nowhere in speech: しょうねん.
notes: 少女 しょうじょ is the girl. Both are written words rather than what you would call a child to their face.
sentence: 少年たちがサッカーをしている。
sentence_meaning: The boys are playing soccer.

mnemonic: 糸 thread wound round and round, and 返す giving it back. Round it comes again, and you are about to say the same sentence for the third time: くりかえす.
notes: Same 返 as 返す かえす. 繰り返し くりかえし is a repetition as a noun.
sentence: 彼女は同じ間違いを繰り返した。
sentence_meaning: She repeated the same mistake.

mnemonic: 我 the self drawn as a hand holding a weapon, and 慢 a heart slowed right down. Keeping still when everything in you says do not. Gah. Man. がまん.
notes: 我慢する is to put up with it. Endurance rather than patience: something is wrong and you are not reacting to it.
sentence: 彼のわがままには我慢できません。
sentence_meaning: I can't put up with his selfishness.

mnemonic: 我 the self, and 々 saying do that one again, so selves in the plural. Said from a podium by somebody speaking for everybody in the room: われわれ.
notes: 々 repeats the character before it, so this is 我我. Formal and a shade grand. 私たち わたしたち is the everyday we.
sentence: 我々の決意は固いです。
sentence_meaning: Our decision is firm.

mnemonic: 咸 all of it landing on 心 a heart, and 覚 the eye that took it in. Below thinking. What your hand knows about the water before you do: かんかく.
notes: 感じ かんじ is the impression; 感覚 is the faculty itself. Same 覚 as 覚える おぼえる.
sentence: 冷えて指の感覚がない。
sentence_meaning: There's no sensation in my cold fingers.

mnemonic: 音 sound down at the bottom with a whole village piled on top of it to bounce off. One door in an empty building and the stairwell has an opinion: ひびく.
notes: Also does words landing: 心に響く こころにひびく is something that resonates.
sentence: このホールは音がよく響きます。
sentence_meaning: Sounds carry well in this hall.

mnemonic: 何 the same what-on-earth as なに, with the answer left deliberately vague. It got done. Nobody is going to explain how, and it is better not to ask: なんとか.
notes: 何とかなる is it will work out somehow. As a request, 何とかして is do something about it.
sentence: 何とかお願いします。
sentence_meaning: Please, I'm begging you.

mnemonic: Three peaks and nothing else to it. Also a pile of anything at all: a 山 of washing, a 山 of work, and neither is going anywhere: やま.
notes: 富士山 ふじさん uses さん. 山 also means a heap, and 山場 やまば is the climax of something.
sentence: 山の空気はきれいだ。
sentence_meaning: The mountain air is clean.

mnemonic: 当 landing squarely on the spot and 前 whatever is right in front of you. So obvious it is not worth the sentence, and saying it out loud is nearly rude: あたりまえ.
notes: Same 当 as 当然 とうぜん, which is the more written version of the same idea.
sentence: あなたの成績が下がったのは当たり前です。
sentence_meaning: No wonder your grades dropped.

mnemonic: 予 beforehand and 定 something settled under a roof. Fixed in advance, which is exactly as much as it promises. Written in pencil: よてい.
notes: 予定通り よていどおり is on schedule, using the 通り you already have. 約束 やくそく is a promise, which binds harder.
sentence: 今日の予定を教えてください。
sentence_meaning: Please tell me what your schedule is for today.

mnemonic: 歹 bare bones with blades beside them, and 念 a heart stuck on 今 this moment. What is left over, and the feeling about it. The bus went as you reached the stop: ざんねん.
notes: 残念ながら opens bad news, meaning unfortunately. It is disappointment rather than apology.
sentence: その試合は残念な結果になった。
sentence_meaning: The result of that game was disappointing.

mnemonic: 辶 the road with somebody already well up it and you coming along behind. Not catching them. The state of being behind and still going: おう.
notes: Same reading as 王 おう, king. 追いかける おいかける is the more active chasing.
sentence: 警官は怪しい男の後を追ったよ。
sentence_meaning: The police officer went after the suspicious man.

mnemonic: 糸 finely woven thread, and 麗 a deer with its antlers drawn out matching. Neat is the point, which is why it does clean as readily as it does lovely: きれい.
notes: Almost always written in kana. 美しい うつくしい is beauty only; きれい covers tidy as well.
sentence: ハインさんは綺麗な人です。
sentence_meaning: Hein-san is a beautiful person.

meaning: to be, to come, to go (honorific form)
mnemonic: The chef looks up, sees who has come in, and the shout goes up before the door has shut. Never about yourself, only about the guest standing there: いらっしゃる.
notes: Honorific, and it stands in for いる, 来る and 行く all at once, so it can mean be, come or go depending on the sentence. いらっしゃいませ, the shout in every shop, is this verb.
sentence: お客様がいらっしゃいました。
sentence_meaning: Your guest has arrived.

mnemonic: New grass 艹 coming up under your right hand 右, days old and already greener than the rest of the field. Nothing on it has had time to go tough: わかい.
sentence: 彼はまだ若いです。
sentence_meaning: He's still young.

mnemonic: Told no three times and she is still in the doorway with her coat on. However it has to happen, whatever it takes, she is going: どうしても.
notes: One of a set built on どう. どうしても is no matter what, どうも is somehow or for some reason, どうせ is anyway.
sentence: どうしてもその訳を知りたい。
sentence_meaning: I really want to know the reason.

mnemonic: The old man has not spoken for a full minute. He is not stuck, he is turning the thing over, and what he finally puts on the table is his: かんがえ.
notes: A worked-out view. 思い おもい is nearer a feeling.
sentence: それは良い考えです。
sentence_meaning: That's a good idea.

mnemonic: The turning went by an hour ago and the road 辶 only runs one way. Whatever was back there is in the ground 土 now: かこ.
sentence: それは過去の話だ。
sentence_meaning: That's in the past now.

mnemonic: Nothing moved and nothing made a sound, but the air at your back has changed and you turn round. Something is there and you knew before you saw it: けはい.
sentence: 後ろに人の気配を感じた。
sentence_meaning: I sensed someone behind.

mnemonic: The whole table has a theory about why she left. The one at the root 本 of it is sitting right there and nobody has asked her: ほんにん.
sentence: それは本人に聞いてください。
sentence_meaning: Please ask the person in question.

mnemonic: You had it worked out on paper. Then the thing itself turns up 見, harder and colder than the version in your head, and there is no arguing with it: げんじつ.
sentence: 現実は予想より厳しかった。
sentence_meaning: The reality was harsher than we expected.

mnemonic: Once the channel is cut 氵 the water never runs any other way again. This is what you put in front of a promise you are not going to break: けっして.
notes: Takes a negative later in the sentence: 決して忘れない, never forget. On its own it is only half a thought.
sentence: このことを決して忘れないでください。
sentence_meaning: Please never forget this.

mnemonic: The pin has been in Africa on his wall for nine years. Ask when and there is no date, only that it is going to happen: いつか.
notes: いつ is when. Adding か blurs it into some time, no date attached.
sentence: 僕はいつかアフリカに行きたい。
sentence_meaning: I want to go to Africa some time.

mnemonic: Boards 木 laid flat under a shelter 广. You never look at it until your socks find the wet patch and you are hopping: ゆか.
sentence: 床がぬれている。
sentence_meaning: The floor is wet.

mnemonic: The yellow 黄 tree 木 came down across the road, not along it. Everything gets measured the way it lies now, side to side: よこ.
sentence: 横の長さは1メートルです。
sentence_meaning: Its width is one meter.

meaning: to rest, to take time off
mnemonic: A man 亻 has stopped walking and put his back against a tree 木, and he is not getting up for anybody. Work can wait until tomorrow: やすむ.
sentence: 昨日、会社を休みました。
sentence_meaning: Yesterday, I took a day off work.

meaning: to turn one's head, to look back on
mnemonic: Halfway down the road 辶 he swings his shoulders round 扌 for one more look at the years behind him. Not going back, only looking: ふりかえる.
sentence: 学生時代を懐かしく振り返ったんだ。
sentence_meaning: I looked back fondly on my school days.

mnemonic: She lives two hours off and the trains were down, and she came anyway, for a forty minute visit. Nobody asked her to do that: わざわざ.
sentence: わざわざ来てくれてありがとう。
sentence_meaning: Thank you for going out of your way to come here.

mnemonic: A mouth 口 in the gateway 門, and it is not letting you through until it has had an answer. Hand up at the back of the room: しつもん.
notes: A question somebody asks. 問題 もんだい is a problem, or a question printed on a test.
sentence: 質問を良く読んでください。
sentence_meaning: Please read the questions carefully.

mnemonic: Lift 興 a thing onto the table and watch who leans in for a taste 味 of it. Some of them will still be there an hour later: きょうみ.
sentence: 私は歴史に興味があります。
sentence_meaning: I'm interested in history.

mnemonic: Huge 巨 strides on tired feet 足 all afternoon, and the bird 隹 that set out with them is somewhere far behind now: きょり.
notes: Distance across space. 間 あいだ is the gap, in time or space or between people.
sentence: 彼らは長い距離を歩き続けたんだ。
sentence_meaning: They kept walking a long distance.

mnemonic: Lift the cover 冂 and there is a valley 谷 under the roof 宀, more in there than the outside promised. Nobody asked for the title: ないよう.
sentence: この本の内容を説明してください。
sentence_meaning: Please explain the contents of this book.

mnemonic: The meeting is in its second hour and your jaw goes before you can stop it, straight across the table from the person talking. You did not decide to do that: つい.
sentence: 会議中、ついあくびをしてしまいました。
sentence_meaning: I inadvertently yawned during the meeting.

mnemonic: One square sits inside another 回 and the outer one keeps going round without ever arriving. The moon has been at it for four billion years: まわる.
sentence: 月は地球のまわりを回っています。
sentence_meaning: The moon revolves around the earth.

mnemonic: Forty people down the pavement outside a ramen shop, shoulder to shoulder 並, and the last one has an hour of this ahead. Nobody breaks it: ならぶ.
sentence: ラーメン屋に沢山の人が並んでいます。
sentence_meaning: There are a lot of people lined up outside of the ramen shop.

mnemonic: The thread 糸 runs out at the end of winter 冬 and you are the one holding the scissors. Homework done, at your own hand, at last: おえる.
notes: 終わる is the thing stopping by itself, 終える is you stopping it. Homework 終わる when the clock runs out and 終える when you finish it. 終わり おわり is the noun, the end itself.
sentence: やっと宿題を終えた。
sentence_meaning: At last I have finished my homework.

mnemonic: He has said nothing rude and still every person at the table has had enough of him. What the heart 心 is doing shows through whatever the mouth says: たいど.
sentence: あの男の態度にみんなあきれてたよ。
sentence_meaning: Everyone was tired of that man's attitude.

mnemonic: It comes out of the ground in two small lumps 金, gets weighed, and ends up on a counter paying for something. This one came to more than he had: かね.
notes: Almost always お金 when you say it. Bare 金 turns up in compounds, where it is usually きん and means gold.
sentence: これはかなり金がかかった。
sentence_meaning: This cost quite a bit of money.

mnemonic: The lid comes down on the day 夜 while you are still standing about in it 今, and there is the moon, better than it has any right to be: こんや.
sentence: 今夜は月がとてもきれいです。
sentence_meaning: The moon is very beautiful tonight.

mnemonic: The day just gone 昨 with its night still attached 夜, and the shooting star that went over it. You will be telling people about that one for a week: ゆうべ.
notes: Read ゆうべ here, not さくや, and often written 夕べ instead. さくや is correct too and sounds stiffer.
sentence: 昨夜、流れ星を見ました。
sentence_meaning: I saw a shooting star last night.

meaning: just as expected, true to one's reputation
